items.title: Resilient navigation of optionally manned TAERO under GNSS-denied conditions
items.summary: An increasing number of unmanned ground vehicles deployed in defence operations are operating in environments where Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are degraded, jammed, or intentionally blocked. Therefore, reliable navigation under such conditions is a critical capability. This study presents the architecture and experimental validation of a resilient navigation system implemented on the TAERO optionally manned ground vehicle. The work focuses on assessing passive navigation modalities under GNSS-degraded and GNSS-denied conditions through real-world field experiments. The study’s contribution of the study lies in its system-level evaluation of the navigation performance and operational limitations of passive sensing modalities on a full-scale optionally manned ground vehicle operating under representative operational conditions. The system integrates a tactical-grade GPS-aided inertial navigation system (INS) with multi-constellation GNSS, wheel odometry, and a forward-mounted vision module.The field experiments were conducted in semi-structured environments with a temporary satellite signal degradation. The INS analysis confirmed stable short-term navigation continuity, but also revealed distance-dependent drift growth, which limits the accuracy of long-duration operations during GNSS outages. To improve the robustness of navigation, a deep learning-based visual odometry approach (DeepVO) was implemented and evaluated using real driving sequences recorded

items.title: Multi-observation robust regression for continuous coastal sea surface height monitoring using GNSS multipath reflectometry
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Global Navigation Satellite System Multipath Reflectometry (GNSS-MR) has substantial potential for coastal sea surface height (SSH) monitoring. Although signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), carrier phase, and pseudorange observations have been used for SSH retrieval, how to fully exploit their complementary information and determine an optimal retrieval strategy remains insufficiently understood. This study develops a multi-observation GNSS-MR framework for SSH retrieval by integrating SNR-based spectral analysis and inverse modeling, single-frequency code-minus-carrier retrieval, and dual- and triple-frequency combinations based on carrier phase and pseudorange observations. A Multi-Observation Robust Regression (MORR) method is further proposed to fuse heterogeneous retrievals within a sliding temporal window while accounting for the second-order dynamic variation of sea level. The results show that carrier-phase-based methods achieve accuracy comparable to SNR-based retrieval, with root mean square errors (RMSEs) below 17 cm and correlation coefficients (R) above 0.98, whereas pseudorange-based approaches yield lower accuracy, with RMSEs of 25.11 and 26.92 cm for dual- and triple-frequency strategies, respectively. The multi-observation strategy substantially enhances temporal coverage, providing an average of 354.66 retrieval timestamps per day and a median sampling interval of 0.038 h. items.title: Assessment of vegetation water dynamics by comparing microwave remote sensing signals from satellites and field-based GNSS reflectometry
items.summary:
Monitoring plant water stress and biomass is limited by labor intensive measurements techniques. Observing plant water conditions more broadly is now enabled by microwave remote sensing. Specifically, satellite-based vegetation optical depth (VOD) provides daily observations of vegetation water volume at tens of kilometers. While satellite VOD has been used for many applications, VOD validations have rarely been carried out. A new method has enabled direct measurements of in-situ VOD, from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS). However, GNSS measurements have yet to be applied to more globally dominant grasslands and shrublands. Here, we explore how satellite-based VOD from SMAP and AMSR-2 compares with field-based microwave observations from 272 GNSS-based interferometric reflectometry (GNSS-IR) sites across the Western US as a part of the Plate Boundary Observatory (PBO) H
                     2 
                    O network. These sensors measure a proxy for VOD, or normalized microwave reflectance index (NMRI), at a much finer scale of tens of meters. We find that satellite VOD is generally positively correlated with GNSS NMRI with correlations between 0.2 to 0.6 across sites. These correlations increase to 0.3 to 0.7 when evaluating sites in regions with more homogenous vegetation types, lower tree cover, and larger seasonal vegetation dynamics. The correlations are higher for X-band VOD, likely related to our findings that X-band VOD and NMRI are both more sensiti

items.title: Visual-Navigation-Aware Multi-UAV Waypoint Assignment for Border Surveillance in GNSS-Denied Environments
items.summary: Abstract Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms using visual navigation methods for border surveillance in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied environments have to maintain positional accuracy with recognisable visual features to reduce the risk of being lost en route. A scarcity of visually rich textures is more likely in rural border environments which makes judicious route planning important for successful visual navigation. Existing multi-UAV routing formulations mainly optimise distance, time, or coverage without deeply considering limited key features terrain for visual navigation. This work formulates a waypoint-assignment problem in which terrain navigability and border surveillance coverage are jointly considered. A terrain navigability framework is constructed from operational orthomosaic imagery using Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) feature density and response quality. Candidate observation positions are extracted from the constructed navigability map and routes are evaluated using an A* planner. The assignment problem is formulated as a single-depot open min--max multiple Travelling Salesman Problem (mTSP) with two objectives: weakest-link route reliability and swarm union border coverage. items.ai_summary: Proposes a visual‑navigation‑aware waypoint assignment for UAV swarms operating in GNSS‑denied border areas. Considers terrain texture scarcity to maintain positional accuracy.

items.title: Research Progress on Multi-Sensor Fusion-Driven Autonomous Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance Technologies for Agricultural Machinery
items.summary: Autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance are key technical foundations for intelligent agricultural machinery operating in open fields, orchards, greenhouses, and mixed human-machine production environments. Single-sensor navigation is constrained by canopy occlusion, dust, vibration, illumination variation, reflective soil surfaces, GNSS multipath, terrain unevenness, and the coexistence of crops, workers, vehicles, animals, and implements. Multi-sensor fusion improves positioning continuity, environmental perception, mapping reliability, and real-time safety decisions by integrating GNSS, inertial measurement units, wheel odometry, LiDAR, RGB cameras, RGB-D cameras, stereo vision, radar, ultrasonic sensors, and crop-row perception. Recent studies have advanced from isolated perception modules toward tightly coupled localization, semantic mapping, trajectory tracking, and dynamic obstacle avoidance. Fusion strategies are becoming more adaptive and uncertainty-aware. However, field deployment still faces challenges in environmental robustness, sensor reliability, real-time computation, and perception–control integration. The review summarizes research progress in sensing foundations, calibration, synchronization, fusion architectures, autonomous navigation, obstacle detection, risk prediction, and local planning. The discussion emphasizes sensor characteristics, algorithmic robustness, agricultural scene complexity, and field-deployable autonomy.
items.ai_summary: Reviews multi‑sensor fusion techniques for autonomous agricultural machinery, highlighting GNSS multipath and integration with vision, LiDAR and inertial sensors for robust navigation.

items.title: A Coastal Erosion Witness Network for Data-Poor Shorelines: Survey-Post and Photogrammetry Accuracy Budgets and Trend-Detection Times
items.summary: Most of the world's eroding shoreline is not monitored by any regular survey, so retreat is often discovered only after houses, wells, paths, or burial grounds have been reached. This paper designs a low-cost witness network for such shorelines — fixed survey posts at 200 m spacing, local observers measuring the position of a defined shoreline proxy (the dune toe, scarp base, or vegetation-line break) on a stated schedule, by tape, by consumer Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver, or by smartphone photogrammetry from marked photo points — and computes what such a network can and cannot establish. From stated error components combined by root-sum-of-squares, the single-measurement standard errors are 0.276 m for tape-and-post, 1.525 m for consumer GNSS, and 0.285 m for smartphone photogrammetry. Once a stated natural shoreline variability of 1.00 m (one standard deviation) around the long-term trend is included, the effective per-observation errors become 1.037 m, 1.823 m, and 1.040 m respectively: natural variability, not instrument precision, dominates the two more precise methods. A least-squares trend analysis (two-sided significance 0.05, power 0.80) then gives, for monthly observations over five years, minimum detectable trends of 0.254 m/yr (tape), 0.446 m/yr (GNSS), and 0.254 m/yr (photogrammetry); over two years the corresponding values are 0.967, 1.700, and 0.970 m/yr. A retreat rate of 0.5 m/yr is confirmed in 3.17 years of monthly tape or photogrammet

items.title: PMSFN: A Multisource Dataset and Model Framework for Tropical Cyclone Wind Speed Retrieval Using GNSS-R and Historical SAR
items.summary: This dataset supports sea surface wind speed retrieval under tropical cyclone conditions by integrating CYGNSS GNSS-R observations, SAR observations and wind products obtained from the CyclObs platform, and IBTrACS best-track records. Following quality control, spatiotemporal collocation, and normalization, each sample combines a current GNSS-R query with spatially neighboring and historical GNSS-R observations and historical SAR scenes. Collocated CyclObs wind retrievals serve as reference labels rather than in-situ measurements.The labeled dataset comprises 184,888 queries from 198 tropical cyclones across the 2020–2026 cyclone seasons. Training, validation, and test sets contain 101,964, 45,214, and 37,710 queries from 108, 48, and 42 cyclones, respectively, with no cyclone overlap between splits. Checkpoint selection uses only the original 34,493-query validation subset; additional validation queries are reserved for reporting. A separate supplement contains 35,940 real unlabeled queries from training cyclones for knowledge distillation. The package includes processed model inputs, reference labels, fixed split definitions, sample identifiers and spatiotemporal metadata, normalization parameters, data-loading and verification utilities, and a partial PMSFN architecture and workflow framework. items.title: Forecasting the ionospheric propagation environment over lightning-active regions: a non-circular machine-learning formulation using NASA ISS-LIS, GNSS TEC and OMNI data
items.summary: Abstract Lightning radiates electromagnetic energy over a very wide frequency range, and the low-frequency component travels to global distances inside the Earth–ionosphere waveguide. How far such a signal reaches, and the highest frequency a given path will carry, are set by the state of the ionosphere at the time of the discharge, which varies by the hour. We forecast that propagation environment over lightning-active regions and convert the forecast into the quantities a radio link actually needs: the F2-layer critical frequency (foF2), the maximum usable frequency (MUF), and the one-hop ground range. A central methodological point is addressed explicitly. Deriving foF2 and MUF from Total Electron Content (TEC) and then training a model to predict them from TEC is circular because the label is a closed-form function of an input feature; any model then recovers R² ≈ 1.0 while learning nothing. We therefore pose the problem as a forecast of TEC at t + ∆t, which is genuinely unobservable at t, and apply the physics to the forecast output rather than to the label. Using 381,858 ISS-LIS flashes, 17,665 fifteen-minute global ionosphere maps, and 8,760 hourly solar and geomagnetic records spanning March–August 2018, five models are compared against a persistence benchmark at 1-, 2-, and 6-hour lead times on a strictly chronological split. All five beat persistence at every lead time. Histogram gradient boosting is the best-performing model, reaching RMSE 3.15 TECU, R² = 0.68, and
items.ai_summary: Machine‑learning model forecasts ionospheric conditions over lightning‑active regions using GNSS TEC, ISS‑LIS and OMNI data, outputting foF2, MUF and one‑hop ground‑wave limits.

items.title: EcoLoc: Arquitetura Híbrida de Localização e Evacuação em Trilhas Sem Conectividade Móvel
items.summary: Resumo: Este artigo apresenta a proposta arquitetural do EcoLoc, um sistema híbrido de orientação em trilhas que busca apoiar a localização lógica do caminhante e o cálculo de rotas de saída em áreas sem conectividade móvel. A arquitetura proposta integra geolocalização por satélite (GNSS), armazenamento local de dados cartográficos, pontos de referência identificados por QR Codes erepresentação da trilha como um grafo ponderado. A leitura de um QR Code permite identificar um checkpoint previamente cadastrado eatualizar a posição lógica do usuário na representação digital do percurso, reduzindo possíveis ambiguidades na identificação debifurcações e segmentos. A partir dessa referência, o algoritmo de Dijkstra poderá calcular caminhos com base nos custos atribuídos aos trechos da trilha. A solução prevê uma aplicação web desenvolvida em Angular, acessível pelo navegador e sem exigência de instalação obrigatória no dispositivo do visitante. A pesquisa fundamenta-se em revisão bibliográ-fica, especificação conceitual da arquitetura e contextualização do Parque EcoBocaina, em Formosa (GO). São definidos critérios para uma futura validação técnica e de campo, incluindo funcionamento offline, identificação de checkpoints, tempo de orientação, leitura de QR Codes, consumo de bateria e adequação das rotas. Como o protótipo ainda deverá ser implementado e avaliado, a eficácia operacional e a viabilidade econômica daproposta permanecem sujeitas a investigação posterior.

items.title: Visible light communication for autonomous vehicle navigation in complex indoor environments
items.summary: Autonomous vehicles operating in complex indoor facilities require reliable position references, vehicle-state exchange, and infrastructure-assisted coordination, particularly where Global Navigation Satellite System coverage is unavailable. This paper presents an integrated Visible Light Communication architecture that uses ceiling-mounted RGBV luminaires, vehicle transceivers, and signaling units to support Lamp-to-Vehicle, Vehicle-to-Vehicle, Vehicle-to-Infrastructure, and Infrastructure-to-Vehicle links. Information is transmitted using On–Off Keying and structured 64-bit frames containing channel identification, position or identification data, timing, and link-dependent operational information. Representative experimental signals illustrate the transmission and recovery of vehicle and infrastructure messages under the considered laboratory conditions. An automated warehouse populated by automated guided vehicles (AGVs) is used as a representative dual-use application scenario. Two complementary simulation studies previously developed by the authors are summarized to demonstrate how VLC-provided information can support traffic coordination. Among signal cycles of 80, 100, and 120s, the 100s setting produced the lowest halting in the considered high-density scenario. A separate arrival-rate analysis identified the central crossing point as the principal bottleneck, with fluid operation at 250AGV/h, operation close to capacity at 500AGV/h, and overload at 750AGV/h. items.ai_summary: Introduces a visible‑light‑communication system to support indoor autonomous‑vehicle navigation where GNSS signals are unavailable, using ceiling‑mounted RGBV luminaires.

items.title: Data and code for "Global elevation models flatten flood-embankment crests, and ICESat-2 photons reduce the regional crest bias of Copernicus GLO-30"
items.summary: This archive holds the derived data and the Python code behind a study of embankment crest heights in global digital elevation models (DEMs). The study has been submitted to Journal of Hydrology. It compares seven global DEMs (Copernicus GLO-30, TanDEM-X EDEM, FABDEM, SRTM, NASADEM, AW3D30 and MERIT) with reference crests. The references are the US National Levee Database on Mississippi River and Tributaries levees, a kinematic GNSS survey of the Koshi River embankment in Nepal, lidar in six other US districts and on the Rhine, and Environment Agency records in the English Fens. It then calibrates GLO-30 crests with ICESat-2 photons alone and tests the calibration once on 49 further regions in England and the US. Finally, it compares DEM crests with the observed 2011 and 2019 Mississippi flood peaks.

items.title: 5,000 Flights to Answer One Question: Can a Drone Sample as Well as a Human?
items.summary: Environmental monitoring still depends on people walking to sampling points with handheld GPS, and published studies show those points are often missed by metres to tens of metres. We asked whether a drone can return to the same sampling point more reproducibly than a person. In simulation, we flew one survey mission with eight sample points 1,000 times in each of five scenarios over our field site at Próspera, Roatán, Honduras, changing only the positioning system the drone steers by and the wind. With RTK GNSS, the median distance between the planned and actual sample point was 3 cm (95th percentile 6 cm). With handheld-grade GPS error, it was 3.3 m in the open and 16.8 m under canopy (95th percentile 34.6 m), in line with published field measurements. A second model of 5,000 out-and-back sampling flights from an edge laboratory gives a median round trip of 3.8 minutes per sample. Positioning, not the platform, decides reproducibility. All results are simulation outputs; a field comparison of drone and hand samples is designed and is the next step. Data, code and figures are openly available. LabGPT Technical Report TR-2026-01. This report accompanies the talk given at Voxel51 Visual AI in Agriculture, 5 November 2026. Data and code: https://github.com/LabGPT-science/5000-flights-drone-sampling

items.title: Methods for monitoring high-rise buildings with allowance for variable stiffness characteristics of structures
items.summary: Purpose. The purpose of the study is to develop an applied approach to integrated monitoring of high-rise buildings for the quantitative assessment of changes in the stiffness of the structural system and for supporting engineering decisions under routine and post-incident operating conditions. Methodology. The study is based on a comparative analysis of GNSS methods, accelerometric and inclinometric monitoring, terrestrial laser scanning, computer vision, SHM and PS-InSAR, as well as on kinematic, modal and stiffness indicators. For consistent interpretation of the results, the sequence "measurement – calculation – interpretation – decision" and an integrated SCI indicator are proposed; this indicator combines global displacements, changes in natural frequencies and the maximum inter-storey drift. Findings. It is shown that the combined analysis of displacements, modal characteristics, inter-storey shifts and equivalent global stiffness provides a more stable diagnostic picture than single-channel monitoring schemes. A demonstration example of a 23-storey building presents the sequence for assessing stiffness changes and interpreting the obtained indicators. Originality. A complete engineering and methodological procedure is proposed for combining kinematic, modal and geometric features within an integrated SHM framework, taking into account the conditions of application in Ukraine. items.title: Reply on RC1
items.summary: Abstract. Atmospheric water vapour is a key greenhouse gas and an important indicator of changes in the hydrological cycle. A three-decade record of GNSS-derived precipitable water vapour (PWV) from five Polish stations of the EUREF Permanent GNSS Network was analysed for the period 1996–2026. The GNSS-derived PWV series were homogenised for documented antenna-configuration changes using ERA5 as a reference and were analysed together with ERA5 PWV. Long-term trends were estimated using harmonic regression with annual and semi-annual components and complemented by non-parametric trend analysis; changes in seasonal amplitude, monthly anomalies, annual PWV maxima, and GNSS–ERA5 consistency were also assessed. Statistically significant positive trends were obtained for the homogenised GNSS series at all five stations, ranging from 0.396 to 0.623 mm decade⁻¹, compared with 0.418–0.598 mm decade⁻¹ for ERA5. At one station, homogenisation changed the estimated GNSS trend from a non-significant 0.200 to a significant 0.424 mm decade⁻¹. Over a nominal 30-year interval, the fitted trends corresponded to PWV increases of 1.189–1.868 mm for GNSS and 1.253–1.795 mm for ERA5. Annual-cycle amplitudes increased at all stations, while trends in annual maxima of daily mean PWV exceeded the corresponding annual-mean trends. items.title: Reply on RC2
items.summary: Abstract. In the auroral ionosphere, plasma turbulence acts as an important dissipation mechanism for magnetospheric energy and the primary cause of radio wave scintillation. Characterizing auroral plasma turbulence across its full spatial extent has historically been limited by the narrow bandwidths of individual instruments. Our investigation approaches the problem of obtaining accurate, scale-dependent information using the physics of the Farley-Buneman (FB) instability, a modified two-stream plasma instability. In this study, we construct a composite spatial powerspectrum of plasma turbulence in the auroral electrojets spanning roughly four orders of magnitude in scale (from ~100 km down to ~20 m). This is achieved by combining a recent Monte-Carlo-based method of spatial clustering of very-high-frequency (VHF) radar echoes, with phase screen information derived from global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals, using ground-based instrumentation in Canada. Through multi-instrument conjunctions with the European Swarm and Japanese Arase missions, we observe that the clustering of electrojet turbulence matches the structuring of field-aligned currents, and correlates with magnetospheric electron fluxes. Statistical analysis of the composite spectra, as well as a very large database of radar clustering spectra only, reveals a consistently steep decay of spectral power in the auroral electrojets, with the most probable spectral index being near −8/3. items.title: Response to Reviewers
items.summary: Abstract. Variability or long-term change in tropopause characteristics has important implications for climate, especially since its temperature – to a large extent – dictates the amount of water vapor (a critical greenhouse gas) in the stratosphere. While conventional observations sufficient for examining tropopause characteristics provide limited geographic coverage, the growing global navigation satellite system radio occultation record provides relatively unlimited geographic coverage continuously since early 2001. This study applies the temperature lapse-rate tropopause (LRT) and potential temperature gradient tropopause (PTGT) definitions to the most recent 23-year radio occultation data period (2003–2025, inclusive) to create robust climatologies and assess long-term changes (statistically significant positive/negative trends) in the altitude, temperature, and sharpness of the primary tropopause and in the occurrence of multiple tropopauses. Regardless of definition, primary tropopause altitudes and temperatures are found to be increasing in most locations globally, consistent with other studies. A narrow region of decreasing tropopause altitudes in the subtropics and over the southern hemisphere east Pacific ocean basin is found to be driven by localized tropical narrowing, while the width of the tropics (based on tropopause altitude) is found to be increasing otherwise, especially throughout the northern hemisphere. items.title: STarlight Acquisition and Reflection toward Interferometry (STARI) mission
items.summary: We introduce the NASA-funded mission STARI (STarlight Acquisition and Reflection toward Interferometry), a two-spacecraft technology demonstrator for future long-baseline interferometers. STARI will perform, to our knowledge, the first in-space transfer of starlight between free-flying spacecraft, a critical step toward long-baseline space interferometry. Two propulsive 8U CubeSats in low Earth orbit will fly in formation with separations up to 200 m: one relays a narrow stellar beam to the other, where an off-axis parabola reimages it into a single-mode fiber. Using differential GNSS, visible LED beacons, and fast-steering mirrors in closed-loop control, we aim to sustain diffraction-limited, high-throughput fiber coupling during formation flight. STARI, targeting launch in 2029, is designed to mature key technologies needed for future mission concepts such as the Large Interferometer for Exoplanets (LIFE), which would seek atmospheric biomarkers on nearby Earth-like exoplanets.
items.ai_summary: Describes NASA’s STARI CubeSat demonstrator, employing differential GNSS for precise formation control to transfer starlight between spacecraft.

items.title: The Limitations on Police Regarding GPS Tracking Devices: A Necessary Hindrance?
items.summary: Article one, Section seven of the Washington Constitution states "no person shall be disturbed in his private affairs, or his home invaded, without authority of law." This section provides greater privacy protection than the United States Constitution. "Examination of the constitutional history of this section reveals that the State Constitutional Convention rejected the language of the federal constitution's Fourth Amendment; instead, the Convention adopted the language. .. to intentionally provide greater protection of individual rights." The problem arises when privacy comes face to face with technological advances, such as Global Positioning System ("GPS") devices. GPS units were first built for military use, but have since become popular in all aspects of today's society. For example, car manufacturers attach GPS units inside cars to locate the vehicle in case it is stolen. GPS units are being attached to level three sex offenders in order to cut down on the number of hours police have to spend monitoring the recipients. Unfortunately, citizens also use GPS systems to stalk other individuals as they drive. GPS tracking will impact the legal rights of millions of citizens. The Supreme Court of Washington became one of the first states to address whether police need a warrant in order to use GPS technology to track a suspect.
items.venue: Computer Law Review and Technology Journal
items.authors: Tenison Craddock
items.ai_summary: Analyzes constitutional limits on police use of GPS tracking devices, discussing privacy implications of GNSS surveillance.

items.title: Afternoon and nighttime differences in IRI-2026 electron-content partitioning over Hainan
items.summary: Abstract. Does replacing the modeled bottomside with a locally observed profile improve total electron content (TEC) estimates? We examine this question at Hainan using 1,666 manually traced ionosonde profiles from 852 dates in 2015–2018 and the International Reference Ionosphere (IRI-2026). We replace the modeled profile below the F2 density peak with the traced bottomside, retain the modeled topside to 1000 km, and compare the original and combined columns with contemporaneous GNSS vertical TEC. Replacement increases overall mean absolute error from 5.064 to 5.898 TECU, but the two sampled local times respond differently. Error rises from 6.305 to 8.440 TECU in the afternoon and falls from 3.808 to 3.325 TECU after midnight. Under their respective integration limits, the modeled afternoon bottomside contains 4.338 TECU more than the traced bottomside on average. This extra lower-column content partly offsets the positive GNSS-minus-combined difference, making the original total closer to GNSS. The opposite responses persist when the two integrals meet at the observed peak height. At Hainan, closer agreement in total TEC can therefore conceal a substantial difference in the lower profile, and introducing that observed profile can expose the discrepancy. These Hainan results show that regional TEC updating needs to assess the upper contribution alongside the observed bottomside, particularly in the afternoon, while accounting for GNSS electron content above 1000 km.
items.ai_summary: Study evaluating IRI-2026 electron content partitioning over Hainan by validating combined ionosonde and topside profiles against GNSS vertical TEC.

items.title: Fooling Local Optimizers: Adversarial Initialization Attacks on LiDAR Localization
items.summary: LiDAR (light detection and ranging) localization is a key component of autonomous driving systems, enabling accurate vehicle pose estimation through optimization-based scan registration methods (e.g., the normal distributions transform algorithm). Existing adversarial attacks mainly target the observation space by manipulating LiDAR point clouds, overlooking another important dependency: the position prior used to initialize the optimizer. In this paper, we identify the initialization space as a previously unexplored attack surface and show that GNSS spoofing can drive LiDAR localization to incorrect local optima. Experiments on the Autoware-CARLA platform reveal a convergence basin of approximately 4 m, beyond which initialization perturbations lead to localization failures. Our analysis of observation-space attacks shows that localization errors induced by LiDAR spoofing exhibit a stable magnitude and a dominant drift direction over time. Leveraging these insights, we propose a cross-space adversarial attack that jointly exploits the initialization and observation spaces by coordinating GNSS spoofing with LiDAR manipulation, demonstrating that coordinated perturbations across sensing modalities can propagate through the complete localization stack. The proposed attack increases the mean localization error by approximately 7 m for A-LOAM and 15 m for HDL-Localizer compared to observation-space attacks alone. items.title: Global TEC Variations during the Unique Geospace Storm of May 10–12, 2024
items.summary: Abstract This study provides a detailed comparative analysis of the global spatiotemporal variations of the ionospheric total electron content (TEC) during the extreme geospace storm of May 10–12, 2024. The analysis was conducted using data from 40 global GNSS stations located in Eastern and Western hemispheres near the 68° W and 112° E meridians. This approach allowed for a direct comparison of the ionospheric response in the western and eastern sectors with high spatial and temporal resolution, avoiding the methodological limitations of global smoothing. In the Western Hemisphere, the geospace storm triggered a strong positive ionospheric storm with a TEC enhancement of over 125 TECU at low and mid-latitudes, as well as an intense super-fountain effect that led to a significant expansion of the equatorial ionization anomaly and an equatorial TEC depletion in the trough region of up to 80 TECU. This positive storm was followed by a widespread negative storm, during which the TEC depletion exceeded 60 TECU. In the Eastern Hemisphere, the ionospheric response was characterized by pronounced latitudinal asymmetry, especially during the recovery phase. At latitudes of 15–60° N, a continuous strong negative storm was observed with a TEC depletion of over 40 TECU, whereas at latitudes of 0°–40° S, following an initial brief drop, a steady TEC enhancement was recorded. items.title: Precision Drone Landing Recognition: ResNext50 Transfer Learning Combined with Hybrid Ensemble Random Forest for Optimal Scene Classification
items.summary: A vision-based landing structure to enhance Global Positioning System (GPS) performance during the final descent phase of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). Instead of relying solely on satellite signals, a camera would be placed on the drone in systematic order to obtain real-time photographs as the drone approaches the landing site. The images above are processed in order to locate a predefined important place which is followed to a target location. Once detected, the organization calculates the positional error between the centre of the marker and the image frame. That error is familiar to a proportional regulation scheme which continuously adjusts the drone's horizontal motion continuously during descent, thus minimizing the positional deviation. Compared with the standard GPS-only method, the vision-based strategy provides additional organic wisdom, especially in the case of signal impairment in alternately dense environments where satellite location might be unreliable. During testing, our model reached 91.31% classification accuracy and brought the average landing error down to just 2.34 centimeters. Although GPS is essential for navigation in general, it is not sufficient for more precise landing. The recommended solution will improve the reliability and safety of UAVs while remaining cost-effective and compatible with the existing UAV platforms.

items.title: Application of the Phase Correction Method in Tracking Modules of Navigation Receivers
items.summary: One of the problems of the tracking modules is their significant inertia in case of narrow bandwidth, which is desirable to mitigate signal noise. The paper describes a method of phase correction, improving accuracy and dynamic characteristics of the tracking process in GNSS receivers. The pivotal idea of the method supposes correction of the phase deviation between the received signal and its local copy at the end of every integration period. This correction is performed directly over the phase accumulator of a DDS system. This approach reduces inertial effects crucially. Application of phase correction method with narrow filter bandwidth is much more efficient when FLL-assisted PLL tracking is used. It is shown that in this case a separate FLL discriminator is not needed, and the resulting filter structure can be significantly simplified.
items.ai_summary: Proposes a phase correction method in GNSS receiver tracking modules to significantly reduce inertia and improve dynamics under narrow loop bandwidths.

items.title: Toward Pseudorange-Based PNT with Starlink: A Mock Fused LEO GNSS Implementation
items.summary:
We present experimental results from Starlink for pseudorange-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), emulating a system that fuses a primary communications mission with a secondary low-Earth orbit (LEO) PNT mission. Legacy global navigation satellite system (GNSS) constellations faceinherent vulnerabilities and signal limitations, prompting growing interest in
  broadband LEO constellations---such as SpaceX's Starlink---for resilient PNT. However, opportunistic use of stand-alone Starlink signals fails to achieve
  GNSS-competitive accuracy due to frame timing irregularities and reliance on uncorrected poor-quality publicly available ephemeris data. To overcome these limitations, we present a mock
  implementation of a fused LEO GNSS architecture. Our method extracts time-of-arrival observables from live Starlink Ku-band downlinks and pairs them with high-fidelity, beam-specific orbit and clock models distributed as if provided natively by the constellation operator. In a field campaign, and despite constraints imposed by consumer-grade receiver hardware, the method
  yields 95% error bounds of 2.33 m horizontally (semi-major axis), 3.37 m vertically, and 11.19 ns in timing, with the actual solution errors falling well within these bounds.
items.ai_summary: Demonstrates pseudorange-based PNT using Starlink signals, evaluating a fused LEO-GNSS framework to address timing irregularities and provide resilient navigation.

items.title: Partial Carrier-Phase Integer Ambiguity Resolution for High Accuracy GNSS Positioning
items.summary: Global navigation satellite systems provide ranging based positioning and timing services. The use of the periodic carrier-phase signals is the key to fast and accurate solutions, given that the inherent ambiguities of the carrier-phase measurements are correctly resolved. The idea of partial ambiguity resolution is to resolve a subset of all ambiguities, which enables faster solutions but does not fully exploit the high precision of the carrier-phase measurements. Theory, methods, and algorithms for partial ambiguity resolution are discussed and analyzed with simulated and real data.

items.title: Monitoring of Antarctic Crustal Movement Based on Precise Point Positioning with Ambiguity Resolution Method
items.summary:
Abstract 
                 High-precision monitoring of crustal motion in Antarctica is of great significance for investigating mass changes of the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS), environmental loading effects, and regional geodynamic processes. Precise Point Positioning (PPP) is an effective positioning technique in environments where reference stations are sparse, and PPP Ambiguity Resolution (AR) has clear advantages over float PPP. In this study, PPP and PPP-AR were respectively applied to process the combined Global Positioning System (GPS) and Galileo observations from eight Multi-Global Navigation Satellite System Experiment (MGEX) reference stations in Antarctica during 2020–2024, thereby obtaining long-term coordinate time series, and wavelet analysis, outlier detection, and time-series reconstruction were utilized to improve the quality of the coordinate time series. Based on the pre-processed coordinate time series, the horizontal velocity field was estimated utilizing least-squares linear fitting, and an Antarctic Plate motion model was constructed based on the rigid plate rotation assumption and Euler vector parameters. The results show that, compared with float PPP, PPP-AR can effectively reduce abnormal jumps and random fluctuations in the coordinate time series. Moreover, PPP-AR improves the average positioning accuracy in the North and East components by 7.80% and 24.65%, respectively. items.title: Impact of map generation methods on GNSS-denied positioning aid enhancement using a wearable, high-accuracy, free spin precession quantum magnetometer
items.summary: The increasing prevalence of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing and jamming as well as the growing need for high accuracy positioning where GNSS is unavailable, i.e., underground and underwater, has motivated the need for alternative positioning augmentation methods. Magnetic map matching using the Earth’s naturally occurring magnetic anomalies is a promising candidate for this task particularly when implemented using the highly stable and sensitive nature of Optically Pumped Magnetometers (OPMs). This work is based on a magnetic mapping survey and positioning enhancement field trial carried out using an OPM integrated into a low Size Weight and Power (SWaP) wearable system. We explore the impact of interpolation algorithm choice and survey line density on magnetic map interpolation error and positioning error when using a particle filter based map matching method. We compare a dual-layer equivalent source model to a Sibson based interpolator over nine magnetic maps and report a reduction in the standard deviation of interpolation errors of up to 42 nT. We examine the relationship between interpolation error and positioning performance, with median 50th percentile radial errors ranging from 2.1 m to 60.0 m depending on map. We report a combined effect in which low survey density both reduces particle filter performance and makes it more susceptible to divergent paths when operating near the boundary of the surveyed area.

Here we focus on Hebi City, China, a typical coal-mining city where these stressors overlap, and use 48 Sentinel-1A SAR images (January 2021–December 2024) to derive a PS-InSAR approximate vertical deformation time series. A representative valid InSAR pixel near the HAHB GNSS station shows temporal evolution broadly consistent with the smoothed GNSS vertical observations (RMSE = 4.46 mm). PCA-FastICA separates statistical spatiotemporal modes, which are interpreted using land-use, precipitation, and groundwater-level data. Subsidence concentrates in Heshan District, parts of Shancheng District, and eastern Xun County, whereas uplift or recovery occurs mainly in Qibin District, the central-southern plain, and areas adjacent to water systems. Three statistical modes are retained: seasonal (IC1), long-term trend (IC2), and short-term anomaly (IC3), with dominant-point proportions of 7.76 %, 83.42 %, and 8.82 %, respectively. These proportions describe the locally dominant mode at sampled points, rather than the contributions of physical drivers. items.title: Three-Dimensional GNSS Water Vapor Tomography for Object-Based Precipitation Precursor Identification in Complex Terrain
items.summary: Conventional water vapor–precipitation studies rely on column-integrated or single-site observations, which cannot capture the three-dimensional (3D) structure of moisture aggregation and its role in precipitation triggering in complex terrain where convective, frontal, and orographic rainfall coexist. Using Ningxia Continuously Operating Reference Station (NXCORS) Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations (2018–2021), we develop a 3D water vapor tomography model (5 km × 6 km × 1 km computational grid; 5 min retrieval interval), validated against independent radiosonde and ERA5 data (r = 0.953/0.881; RMSE = 1.998/1.949 g m−3). We propose 3D Water Vapor Preferential Zones (WVPZs) and an object-based framework using stratified dual-percentile thresholds (99%/97%) and 3D connected-component tracking to identify, track, and match WVPZs with rainfall regions under temporal (≤6 h prior) and spatial (≤100 km centroid distance) constraints. Across 16 events, WVPZs were present in 94.97% of 5 min time steps. In 416 matched pairs, WVPZs typically formed 2–6 h before rainfall, with a mean precursor time lag of 231.5 min at onset. Mean centroid distances were 52–55 km (mean minimum centroid distance: 39.4 km). By rainfall type, convective rainfall had the shortest precursor time lag (220.6 min) but largest distance (55.7 km); frontal rainfall showed the tightest coupling (49.1 km); orographic rainfall had the longest precursor time lag (254.0 min). items.title: GNSS Technologies for the Sustainable Energy Sector: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
items.summary: This article presents a comprehensive overview of the applications of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) in the energy sector. Based on 161 publications selected from the Web of Science database, it outlines the role of measurement techniques such as RTK/RTN (Real-Time Kinematic/Network), PPP (Precise Point Positioning), GNSS-R/IR (GNSS Reflectometry/Interferometric Reflectometry), and GNSS-RO (GNSS Radio Occultation) in monitoring critical infrastructure such as wind farms, solar installations, hydroelectric dams, and nuclear power plants. The reviewed studies show that GNSS improves the performance of solar tracking systems in photovoltaics, enables automated drone inspections of difficult-to-access components, and provides time references for critical synchronisation, e.g., via the Precision Time Protocol (PTP), in smart grids. Combined with other measurement techniques, GNSS enables precise monitoring of deformations of large dams and multi-kilometre pipelines. The main barriers identified include limited sky visibility, multipath errors, jamming, and spoofing. These phenomena are important from a security perspective in the energy sector, particularly in the nuclear sector. The development of multi-constellation GNSS (GPS, Galileo, and BeiDou) and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) are identified as key factors for improving the resilience and continuity of modern energy systems.

items.title: Ultralight scalar field domain walls and Galileo GNSS atomic clocks
items.summary: In this article, we study the impact of an Earth-sized ultralight scalar field domain wall (DW) on the European Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System constellation and the feasibility of a related detection. In particular, a set of statistical procedures is developed and implemented to characterize the statistical properties of the background noise for a subnetwork of $N$ Galileo satellite clocks, including a false-alarm rate estimation and a detection efficiency analysis. These methods allow to implement a coincidence analysis and establish a preliminary statistical framework for a robust and controlled search for domain-wall crossings in clock data, and for deriving constraints on the associated fundamental particle physics parameters. The activity is addressed from the point of view of the scientific objectives of the Galileo for Science (G4S$\_2.0$) project.

items.title: Extending Geodetic Estimation Theory by Factor Graph Optimization: A Case Study on GNSS-PPP
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   This paper aims to bridge the gap and exploit the duality between geodetic estimation theory and Factor Graph Optimization (FGO), a powerful estimation framework which has been developed within the robotics community. We first show the geodetic perspective on large least-squares problems, reviewing well-established solution strategies such as the normal equations method, the orthogonalization method, and parameter elimination. We then establish the factor graph perspective using the example of GNSS PPP, and show how the structure of the probabilistic graphical model directly relates to the structure of the design matrix and reveals its sparse structure. We then show how the graphical model supports the estimation process and how the graph structure facilitates exploiting sparsity for solving large-scale least squares problems efficiently. The paper concludes with a synthesis of insights and implications for general geodetic estimation approaches.

items.summary: Accurate estimation of the effective operational area of automatic transplanters is essential for evaluating machinery productivity, improving field management efficiency, and supporting digital agricultural applications. However, operational-area estimation based on low-cost BeiDou trajectories remains challenging because raw trajectories are often affected by positioning uncertainty, trajectory discontinuities, and non-productive machine movements, including headland turning, road transportation, empty transfer, and seedling loading/unloading operations. Directly using all recorded trajectories may therefore introduce considerable area overestimation, whereas excessive trajectory filtering may remove valid productive operations. This study proposes a state-aware hierarchical trajectory fusion framework coupled with a low-cost BeiDou-based monitoring system for automatic operation-state recognition and operational-area estimation of transplanters. Unlike conventional trajectory-processing approaches that mainly focus on geometric smoothing or spatial clustering, the proposed framework jointly considers positioning reliability, motion consistency, spatiotemporal continuity, and operational semantics to extract productive transplanting trajectories from noisy GNSS observations. Three field datasets containing more than 49,000 trajectory points (approximately 30,000 valid records after preprocessing) were collected from automatic transplanters operating in Xinjiang, China. items.summary: A Filter with No Tuning against EKF2 and EKF3 Tuned on the Truth, Pre-registered Simulation Syntonic Nav takes every noise, prior and gate of a navigation filter from records of the sensors; nothing in it is tuned. In its version 2.0, its latest form, SYN5 v4b, was compared with PX4's EKF2 and ArduPilot's EKF3 at their shipped default values, and held all 30 sealed checks. That comparison leaves open whether the advantage is only the defaults' mismatch with the vehicle. This note answers it with the strongest rivals the bench allows: EKF2 and EKF3 whose noise, bias and gate parameters were tuned against the true state, an oracle no human tuner has, on the same kinds of scenario they were then tested on. Eleven parameters of EKF3 and eleven of EKF2 were searched in log space on spent seeds; the tuned sets, the criteria and written predictions were frozen; one confirmation ran on 20 fresh seeds over 14 scenarios and was judged once. SYN5 v4b, unchanged, held 39 of the 42 criteria. It diverged in none of 280 runs, while the truth-tuned EKF3 diverged on 4 of 20 seeds with a faulty IMU and the truth-tuned EKF2 on all 20. items.title: Adaptive Robust Visual-Inertial Localization Method in GNSS-Denied Environments
items.summary: With the rapid development of smart wearable devices and autonomous systems, high-precision and highly robust positioning in GNSS-denied environments—such as indoor spaces, underground areas, and tunnels—has become a critical engineering requirement. Nevertheless, several key challenges remain in practical applications. This paper establishes an adaptive and robust visual-inertial pedestrian navigation algorithm framework. For the inertial sensor, an online error compensation model is constructed, and IMU preintegration is employed to achieve pedestrian motion propagation. For visual observations, a lightweight front-end is designed to reduce computational burden. By introducing the Huber robust kernel function, the quality of visual observation information is evaluated in real time, and anomalous residuals are down-weighted or even rejected, thereby preventing abnormal observation data from degrading the state estimation and significantly enhancing the stability of the system in complex environments. Validation in real-world scenarios demonstrates that the proposed algorithm achieves a positioning error of less than 0.4% in normal environments while maintaining a positioning error within 1.5% in visually degraded scenarios, exhibiting excellent anti-degradation capability and good engineering applicability.

items.title: Stochastic Model Refinement for Multi-GNSS Real-Time PPP Based on Orbit and Clock Extrapolation Error Statistics
items.summary: Short-term outages of real-time state space representation (SSR) products degrade precise point positioning (PPP) accuracy. We propose a multi-GNSS PPP stochastic model refinement method based on historical statistics of additional signal-in-space range error (SISRE). System-level and satellite-level age-dependent models are constructed offline from joint range-domain statistics of orbit and clock extrapolation errors. Online, model outputs are converted into equivalent additional variances for direct variance inflation (DVI). Thirty days of Wuhan University SSR data are divided into non-overlapping 15-day training and test sets for modeling and cross-day validation. Within 10 min, BDS-3 and Galileo show relatively small extrapolation errors, GPS shows pronounced inter-satellite differences, and GLONASS shows higher overall errors. The training model and test reference model show similar error scales and age-dependent growth, indicating cross-day repeatability. Without additional downweighting, four-constellation simulated kinematic PPP experiments with 10 min outages yield a three-dimensional root mean square (3D RMS) positioning error of 13.26 cm. System-level and satellite-level DVI reduce this to 4.33 and 4.07 cm, respectively, corresponding to reductions of approximately 67% and 69%. items.title: Point-Adaptive Detector Selection and Alert Confirmation for Dam GNSS Displacement Monitoring
items.summary: Thresholds calibrated on historical data produce excessive false alarms when conditions change, and field-confirmed abnormal events are too scarce to supervise alarm calibration. This study develops a point-adaptive detector selection and alert confirmation workflow for dam Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) displacement monitoring. At each of nine monitoring points, a dual gate screens fifteen candidate anomaly detectors into a small point-specific ensemble, and a four-level confirmation policy—M-of-N temporal persistence, weighted detector support, an independent displacement-band escalation path, and event aggregation—converts the score into auditable alerts for engineering verification rather than a prediction of future instability. On an eighteen-month, nine-point GNSS record, the confirmation policy applied to the single detector retained at all nine points (TCN-AE) detects 68.1% of chronologically injected events, and the point-adaptive fused ensemble detects 66.7% across all nine points (block-bootstrap 95% confidence interval (CI) 51.4–81.9%), with a cleaned-negative alarm rate of 0.0045% and 99.98% precision on the cleaned negative class (full-negative-class false-positive rate (FPR) 0.09% as an upper bound; precision 99.68% as a lower bound, dominated by correctly flagged operational episodes); the prevalence-adjusted positive predictive value is about 41% at a 0.1% operational prevalence. items.title: Robust GPS/Visual–Inertial Navigation in Dynamic and GPS-Degraded Environments via Dynamic Feature Masking and GPS Measurement Screening
items.summary: Achieving reliable localization in dynamic environments remains challenging because moving objects corrupt visual constraints, and degraded GPS measurements introduce erroneous absolute-position corrections. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust GPS/visual–inertial navigation (VIO) framework that enhances the reliability of visual and GPS measurements at the measurement level without modifying the underlying VIO estimator. In the visual front end, a YOLOv8-based detector asynchronously processes downsampled images to identify potentially dynamic regions, which are subsequently mapped back to the original resolution to generate a dynamic mask. Features detected within these masked regions are excluded from subsequent visual state estimation. For GPS integration, receiver-provided latitude, longitude, and altitude (LLA) coordinates are first transformed into a local East-North-Up (ENU) frame. Temporally aligned initial segments of the GPS and VIO trajectories are then used to estimate the relative yaw rotation between the two coordinate frames, thereby expressing GPS positions directly within the VIO frame. Prior to each GPS update, a two-stage screening strategy combining receiver-reported covariance with normalized innovation squared (NIS) testing rejects position measurements exhibiting excessive uncertainty or statistical inconsistency with the VIO state prediction. items.title: A Station-Specific Regional Approach to Improve Galileo Single-Frequency Ionospheric Corrections over Europe
items.summary: The European Galileo constellation employs the NeQuick-G model to provide ionospheric corrections for single-frequency positioning. This study proposes an improved correction algorithm that incorporates local ionospheric characteristics obtained from Digisondes and collocated GNSS receivers across Europe. The developed algorithm supports long-term, short-term, and real-time applications, with this study focusing on evaluating its real-time performance using retrospective data collected at 10 European stations between 2014 and 2023. In the proposed approach, station-specific CCIR coefficients are updated every five minutes using automatically scaled foF2 and M(3000)F2 measurements from local Digisondes. Additionally, the NeQuick-G effective ionization parameter (Az) is optimized using Total Electron Content (TEC) observations recorded by local GNSS receivers on the preceding day. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm generally provides more accurate ionospheric corrections than the standard NeQuick-G model, particularly during periods of high solar activity, achieving reductions in root mean square error (RMSE) of up to 3 TECU. Under moderate-to-low solar activity and at higher latitudes, improvements are less pronounced, with both approaches exhibiting comparable performance.

items.title: Detecting GPS Spoofing Attacks with a Trust Index Using Sensor Cross-Validation Based on Inertial Information
items.summary: GPS spoofing poses a critical threat to autonomous mobile robots that rely on unencrypted civilian GPS signals for navigation. Although the PX4 autopilot’s extended Kalman filter (EKF2) incorporates innovation gating to reject anomalous measurements, spoofed signals that emulate legitimate GPS characteristics with low reported error metrics can bypass this defense. This paper presents a sensor cross-validation framework that detects GPS spoofing by cross-validating the reported GPS solution against the inertially propagated state estimate. Eight heuristic detection rules are evaluated as a training-free baseline, while the Random Forest classifier primarily exploits GPS accuracy and EKF2 innovation features. Ground-truth annotations for training and evaluation are taken from the simulator’s known spoofing timelines across 60 synthetic flights, independently of the heuristic rules themselves. A Random Forest classifier trained on 30-sample sliding windows (15-sample stride) across 34 telemetry fields achieves 99.8% classification accuracy with a spoofed-class F1-score of 0.997 on a dataset of 7920 labeled windows collected from 60 simulated flights across three terrain types in the PX4 SITL–Gazebo environment under varied wind and spoofing conditions. The proposed GPS Trust Index provides a continuous real-time integrity metric complementary to the binary classifier output. items.title: A Phase-Balanced Differential Rydberg-Atom Quantum Receiver for Weak GNSS Signal Detection
items.summary: This paper proposes a phase-balanced differential Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (DRAQR) for weak-signal recovery, using local-oscillator phase control to reinforce differential signal responses and a shared squeezed-reservoir model to correlate inter-cell quantum projection noise (QPN) and photon shot noise (PSN). An analytical model incorporating QPN, PSN, intrinsic thermal noise (ITN), and inter-cell correlations quantifies signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain, outage-constrained minimum detectable power, and bit-error rate (BER) for square $M$-QAM. For the evaluated settings, SNR gain reaches approximately $10$~dB as PSN correlation approaches unity, with BER decreasing as correlation increases. Under Rician fading, at a $0$-dB threshold SNR and maximum outage probability of $0.1$, the minimum detectable power decreases from $-146.95$~dBm at $K=1.155$ to $-159.98$~dBm at $K=2.4$. Analytical results are validated against Monte-Carlo simulations over $150{,}000$ data runs per point for receiver-performance plots.

items.title: An Inspection Game for Monitor Design Against GNSS Timing Attacks in Synchronous Islanding
items.summary: Phasor measurement units (PMUs) take their time from GNSS, so a spoofer that slowly drags a receiver clock rotates the reported phase without touching the power waveform. The threat is acute in synchronous islanding, where a controller keeps an islanded generator in phase with the grid, using one PMU on each side of an open breaker, so that the two can be reconnected at any moment: a differential clock bias of about $0.56$\,ms can make the controller hold the generator $10^\circ$ out of phase while it reports perfect synchronism. We cast the defense as a zero-sum inspection game. The defender, as inspector, chooses its timing monitors and audits the clocks periodically; the attacker, as inspectee, drags the two clocks to an unsafe bias by the next audit; the payoff is the evidence, the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the probability laws of the defender's record under attack and under normal operation. Our central result is that the evidence equals the cost of the cheapest innocent explanation of the attacked record. This single identity predicts which monitors work, turns the attacker's best response into a strictly convex quadratic program, and turns the defender's design into a convex program with a saddle point.                    Reliable fiducial stations form the foundation of regional and national geodetic reference frames, requiring long-term coordinate stability and well-characterized stochastic behaviour. Although continuous Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) networks are increasingly used for geodetic applications, objective methodologies for evaluating the suitability of individual stations as fiducial references remain limited. This study presents an integrated framework for assessing the vertical-component fiducial suitability using multi-year GNSS position time series. Daily Precise Point Positioning (PPP) solutions were generated with GipsyX software [Bertiger W, Bar-Sever Y, Dorsey A, Haines B, Harvey N, Hemberger D, et al. GipsyX/RTGx, a new tool set for space geodetic operations and research. Adv Space Res 2020;66:469–89] and analysed for 66 continuously operating reference stations in Uttar Pradesh, India, spanning March 2022 to December 2025. Of the total of 66 continuous GNSS stations initially considered, one station (KASH) had insufficient data for time-series assessment, leaving 65 stations for classification. Only data quality, residual variability, deterministic model fit, and stochastic uncertainty contributed to the classification. Other estimated parameters are presented for completeness and discussion but were not used as classification criteria. items.title: A cross-epoch ambiguity tracking method for GNSS/INS/Vision-based urban navigation
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   High-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning in urban environments is frequently degraded by carrier-phase interruptions and cycle slips, leading to repeated ambiguity reinitialization and prolonged reconvergence after signal reacquisition. To address this challenge, a Cross-Epoch Ambiguity Tracking (CEAT) method is proposed for tightly coupled GNSS/Inertial Navigation System (INS)/Vision navigation. The converged ambiguities are preserved across discontinuous carrier-phase arcs and reused after signal reacquisition for cycle-slip detection and ambiguity rectification. Carrier-phase residuals are constructed using the stored ambiguities and propagated pose, enabling residual-based cycle-slip detection and Least-squares AMBiguity Decorrelation Adjustment (LAMBDA)-based integer estimation. The affected ambiguities and their corresponding uncertainties are then rectified according to the resolved cycle slips, thereby accelerating ambiguity convergence and improving positioning performance. The proposed method is evaluated using simulated cycle-slip tests and real-world urban and campus datasets. Comparisons with representative cycle-slip detection methods and sliding ambiguity window frameworks demonstrate the effectiveness of CEAT in cycle-slip detection, ambiguity rectification, and positioning performance. items.title: On the Error Distribution in Precise Levelling Sections
items.summary: The assumption that measurement errors follow a Gaussian (normal) distribution is widely accepted in geodesy and related sciences. However, numerous studies over the past decades have reported observational evidence that challenges this assumption, particularly using modern measurement techniques such as Global Navigation Satellite Systems, Satellite Laser Ranging, gravimetry, and astronomical observations. Earlier investigations from the mid - 20th century also indicated deviations from normality in precise and hydrostatic levelling data.This study examines the statistical properties of levelling discrepancies from several national levelling campaigns: the Second Levelling of Bulgaria (1953 – 1957), the Third Levelling of Bulgaria (1975 – 1984), the Second Levelling of Finland (1935 – 1955), and the Third Levelling of Finland (1978 – 2006). The analysis focuses on testing the normality of the discrepancies using statistical measures of skewness and excess kurtosis, as well as chi - squared goodness - of - fit tests. The results reveal significant deviations from normality across all datasets examined. items.title: Over-injection of time-correlated tropospheric constraints induces PPP height shifts: a Gauss–Markov remedy
items.summary: Abstract External zenith total delay (ZTD) constraints improve precise point positioning (PPP) but are commonly treated as temporally independent epoch-wise pseudo-observations. Their errors exhibit substantial temporal correlation. Neglecting this correlation can over-inject constraint information and distort PPP height through its strong coupling with ZTD. This study uses ZTD derived from the fifth-generation European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis (ERA5) to quantify the resulting height effects. Treating the ZTD constraint errors as white noise overestimates their effective information content by a factor of about 65 relative to that implied by the residual autocorrelation, while the magnitude of the ZTD-to-height leakage coefficient reaches 1.74 in static mode and 1.93 in kinematic mode. To handle this temporal correlation, the constraint residuals are modeled as a combination of a diurnal cycle, a daily constant offset, and a time-correlated component described by a first-order Gauss–Markov process, with the constant offset and the Gauss–Markov process introduced as additional filter states. Results show that the proposed approach not only retains the convergence gain over the unconstrained solution but also substantially mitigates the constraint-induced height shifts. items.title: Deep learning and adaptive carrier Phase–Doppler weighted fusion for GNSS cycle slip detection and repair
items.summary: Abstract Cycle-slip detection and repair is a critical preprocessing step in high-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning. Under varying cycle-slip ratios, detection thresholds are difficult to determine adaptively, leading to missed detections, false alarms, and suboptimal repair. This paper proposes a deep-learning cycle-slip detection and repair method based on Satellite- and Epoch-Differenced (SDED) observations and develops an adaptive Phase-Doppler (PD) weighted fusion mechanism for kinematic observations. The SDED representation suppresses common-mode errors and highlights cycle-slip signatures. A cycle slip is detected when the prediction residual exceeds the detection threshold, and the rounded residual is used directly as the repair correction. For kinematic observations, PD residuals provide complementary physical consistency information and are adaptively fused with the deep-learning decision through a noise quality factor weighting scheme to suppress false alarms. Bayesian optimization is used to tune the model parameters, and the Transformer, CNN, and LSTM are benchmarked against the Time-Differenced Carrier Phase (TDCP) method across different frequencies, observation modes, and cycle-slip ratios. The Transformer achieves the best overall performance, with detection success rates consistently above 99% and repair success rates above 97% under static conditions, and mean repair errors below 0.11 cycles. items.title: Probabilistic Assessment of Cooperative Positioning Accuracy for a UAV Group...
items.summary: When satellite signal reception is interrupted, the inertial navigation error of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) increases. Inter-vehicle communication allows a UAV that has successfully acquired satellite coordinates to be used to correct the position of other members of the group. The objective of this study is to evaluate how the size of the group, the probability of acquiring satellite coordinates, and the duration of the observation period affect the calculated error in cooperative positioning. A probabilistic model is employed, assuming that the acquisition of satellite coordinates by different UAVs occurs as independent events over successive one-minute intervals. The root-mean-square error (RMSE) is calculated for two scenarios: one where a “coordinate anchor” (a reference point with a defined cooperative correction error) is available, and one where it is absent – in which case the inertial navigation error grows quadratically. Given a 0.1 probability of a single UAV acquiring satellite coordinates within a one-minute interval and an observation period of 5 minutes, the calculated error is 269.05 m for a single UAV, 27.57 m for a group of ten, and 11.51 m for a group of twenty. Under the assumed parameters, further increasing the group size causes the error to converge toward the cooperative correction level of 11.37 m. items.title: A Multimodal Perception Unmanned System Based on GNN and SLAM
items.summary: The complex environments encountered in emergency rescue scenarios pose severe challenges to the perception and navigation capabilities of unmanned ground systems. This paper designs and implements a ground unmanned rescue system named "SkyEye" based on multimodal perception fusion. The system adopts a four-wheel independent steering and four-wheel drive (4WIS-4WID) omnidirectional ground chassis and integrates a 4D-FMCW LiDAR, structured-light binocular cameras, a high-precision IMU, and Beidou RTK. Through a tightly coupled graph-optimization SLAM framework and GNN-based dynamic obstacle prediction, it achieves robust perception and autonomous navigation in complex rescue scenarios. Experiments show that under clear open-field conditions, the system achieves centimeterlevel positioning accuracy and obstacle recognition accuracy ≥95%. In extreme dense smoke, recognition accuracy remains at 82.6% with stable navigation. The obstacle avoidance response latency is ≤0.5 s in narrow spaces and GNSS-denied tunnels. This paper elaborates the platform kinematic model, multi-sensor spatio-temporal calibration, detailed SLAM implementation, and complete GNN trajectory prediction pipeline, providing a theoretical basis and engineering reference for ground emergency rescue unmanned systems.

items.title: Research on Intelligent Switching and Control Strategy of Air-Sea Amphibious WIG Craft Based on Multi-Sensor Fusion
items.summary: Aiming at the core problems of abrupt changes in dynamic characteristics and poor smoothness in mode switching during the cross-medium operation of amphibious wing-in-ground (WIG) craft, this paper develops an intelligent switching and control system based on multi-sensor fusion. The system integrates measurement data from the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) to construct a state observation module for mode switching decision-making. On this basis, a fuzzy switching logic centered on flight altitude and sea state characteristics is proposed, and a hybrid control strategy combining Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) is designed to realize the smooth transition between water surface and flight modes. Numerical simulations conducted in Python demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can accurately determine the mode switching timing, stabilize the pitch angle fluctuation within ±3° during the transition process, and effectively enhance the ability of WIG craft to operate autonomously and stably of the WIG craft in complex sea conditions.

items.title: UAV Orthomosaic Imagery and U-Net Vegetation Classification Map, Minidoka National Wildlife Refuge, Idaho, 2025
items.summary: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with U-Net, a convolutional neural network for image segmentation, was used to produce a 0.25 m-resolution vegetation classification map across approximately 638 ha (area of interest [AOI] bounding extent; ~345 ha mapped) of burned sagebrush steppe at Minidoka National Wildlife Refuge, Idaho. Red-green-blue (RGB) imagery was acquired on 8 July 2025 using a WingtraOne Gen 2 UAV with an RGB61 camera at approximately 107 m above ground level (~0.02 m ground sampling distance), geotagged with Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) corrections from an Emlid Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) base station and Post-Processed Kinematic (PPK) post-processing, and orthomosaicked in WebODM. Field-collected polygon training and validation labels (244 polygons) were used to train a U-Net convolutional neural network (PyTorch) to classify the imagery into eight vegetation and ground-cover classes: crested wheatgrass (AGCR; Agropyron cristatum), big sagebrush (ARTR; Artemisia tridentata), cheatgrass (BRTE; Bromus tectorum), mixed cheatgrass and Russian thistle (BRTE_SATR; Bromus tectorum + Salsola tragus), thickspike wheatgrass (ELLA; Elymus lanceolatus), Sandberg bluegrass (POSE; Poa secunda), rock/bare ground (ROCK), and Russian thistle (SATR; Salsola tragus). This data release includes the UAV orthomosaic imagery, the filtered classified vegetation map, raw and confidence prediction rasters, and the field-collected training/validation polygons.

items.title: Robust Joint RTT RSS Indoor Localization Using Particle Swarm Optimization
items.summary: Achieving reliable indoor positioning in GNSS-denied environments poses significant challenges due to multipath, interference, signal variability, and hardware-induced biases. In this paper, we propose a novel robust fusion algorithm that jointly estimates user position using Wi-Fi Round Trip Time (RTT) and Received Signal Strength (RSS) data measurements. In addition to joint positioning, the algorithm estimates RTT-driven biases. Unlike conventional algorithms that rely on Gaussian noise assumptions and require RTT data calibration in multi-sensor integration frameworks, our approach implements a weighted negative log-likelihood (NLL) cost function with particle swarm optimization (PSO) that adopts non-Gaussian noise models to capture the non-Gaussian characteristics of RTT signals. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 64% reduction in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and a 66% improvement in 95th percentile localization error compared to weighted nonlinear least squares trilateration. The algorithm is deployed using a single smartphone application enabling an accurate, calibration-free, and low-complexity indoor positioning system suitable for real world applications such as indoor navigation and asset tracking.

items.title: Closing Hormuz Without Closing It: Operational Openness and Risk-Mediated Sovereignty
items.summary: Debate about the Strait of Hormuz usually asks whether Iran can close it, how long a military blockade could last, and how far oil prices would rise. This framing treats closure as a visible physical event and openness as its simple absence. The 2026 disruption exposed the limits of that binary. Commercial passage can collapse even when a navigable channel remains and no actor maintains a complete naval barrier. Insurance may be withdrawn or repriced beyond commercial tolerance, satellite navigation and vessel identification may become unreliable, sanctions and port rules may make a lawful voyage unusable, and seafarers may be unable or unwilling to enter a warlike area. This viewpoint introduces the concept of operational openness, defined as the practical capacity to complete safe, lawful, insurable, informationally reliable, and adequately crewed transit. It also proposes \emph{risk-mediated sovereignty} to describe authority exercised by shaping the conditions under which others decide that passage is possible. At Hormuz, this authority is distributed across coastal states, naval forces, insurers, reinsurers, shipping firms, data providers, ports, regulators, and maritime labour institutions. The article argues that freedom of navigation must therefore be governed as an infrastructural achievement rather than treated only as a legal entitlement or military objective. items.title: Fault-Free Protection Levels, Multi-Receiver Monitoring and Galileo Redundancy for GBAS-Type Differential GNSS at a Reference Station with Real Code Faults
items.summary: Integrity of GBAS relies on the protection levels based on the broadcast error models and on-ground monitors employing comparisons of multiple reference receivers. The former and latter were considered for an Istanbul reference station under real, independently marked code jumps from the GPS. In total, 60,269 smoothed test epochs were considered from a 23.8 km station pair where the fault-free vertical protection level according to the ICAO Annex 10 of the error model data tails covered the error at each epoch; with the use of standard error models, the protection level was violated at 20 epochs for the weighted least squares but the error did not exceed the 10 m alert limit. Under the two to four simulated reference receivers, the B-value monitor was able to detect almost all 20 m single-receiver jumps, hence user-side exclusion and robust estimation were mostly relevant for the case of single-receiver stations and unmonitored faults. Incorporation of Galileo resulted in the reduction of the median VDOP at Istanbul Airport from 1.48 to 1.10 and in the improvement of correct exclusion of two simultaneous faults inserted in the real smoothed code from 59% to 95%. Also, the rare Galileo E1 code deviations of about one chip length at signal acquisition were registered by the reference station; the exclusion kept the vertical effect of the deviation under 4 m, while without exclusion the impact was about 100 m.
