items.title: Odyssey: An automotive lidar-inertial odometry dataset with GNSS-denied situations
items.summary: The development and evaluation of Lidar-Inertial Odometry (LIO) and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems require a precise reference trajectory. The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is often used as a foundation for this, but its signals can be unreliable in obstructed environments due to multi-path effects or loss-of-signal. While existing datasets compensate for sporadic GNSS loss by incorporating Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) measurements, the commonly used systems do not permit prolonged study of GNSS-denied environments due to accumulated drift. Consequently, existing automotive benchmarks are typically restricted to short GNSS-denied segments. To close this gap, we present Odyssey, an automotive LIO dataset featuring: (1) prolonged, previously unseen GNSS-denied environments with reference trajectories enabled by a navigation-grade Ring Laser Gyroscope (RLG)-based RTK/INS; (2) a large and diverse collection of 36 sequences that range from rural outdoor environments to urban and indoor scenarios; and (3) experimentally validated uncertainties, allowing for precise quantification of reference error. Besides providing data for LIO, Odyssey also supports place recognition tasks through threefold trajectory repetition and integration of external mapping data via precise geodetic coordinates. All data, dataloader and supplementary material are available online at https://odyssey.uni-goettingen.de/ .
items.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research

items.title: Modernization of Palestine’s national geodetic reference frame through PAL-GRF2023
items.summary: Abstract Accurate spatial data, which encompasses precise mapping, effective land management, and robust Geographic Information Systems (GIS), is essential for national development. Acknowledging this necessity, the Palestinian Land Authority (PLA) launched a significant initiative to create a contemporary geodetic framework. The existing geodetic networks in Palestine are remnants from the British Mandate period, rendering them severely outdated and insufficient for the current requirements of spatial data. This shortcoming obstructs the generation of precise cadastral and topographic maps and hampers the smooth integration of spatial information into critical land information systems. The "Development of the Palestinian National Geodetic Framework (PAL-GRF)" project entailed the establishment of 10 new local stations throughout the West Bank, each equipped with forced centering steel pillars. These stations were connected with fiducial stations from the International GNSS Service (IGS) and ITRF2020 networks to guarantee global consistency. Engineers from the Palestinian Land Authority performed extensive GNSS observations, with each station being observed simultaneously for a minimum of 8 hours. All data underwent rigorous processing utilizing the Bernese GNSS Software (BSW52) and products from the CODE analysis center. items.ai_summary: Describes the creation of a modern geodetic reference frame for Palestine (PAL‑GRF2023) to improve cadastral mapping and GIS accuracy.

items.title: Sky Region Recognition and Polarization Orientation via Multi-Scale Gradient Connected-Component Extraction for a Bio-Inspired Sensor
items.summary: Sky-region recognition using a bio-inspired polarization sensor helps reduce occlusion-induced errors in polarization orientation and supports applications such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) non-line-of-sight error mitigation and atmospheric irradiance estimation. However, retaining usable sky measurements while rejecting non-sky interference remains challenging in scenes with extensive occlusions. This paper proposes a sky-region recognition and polarization orientation method that combines multi-scale grayscale gradients with connected-component extraction. Multi-scale gradients are computed from the grayscale image derived from the polarization measurements. Gradient, intensity, and degree of polarization (DOP) thresholds are then combined to obtain an initial binary sky mask. Connected-component analysis is then performed, and the largest component is retained as the final mask, which is used to select the polarization measurements for heading estimation. Experimental results on the unmanned platform in scenes containing building, vegetation, and pedestrian occlusions show that the proposed algorithm achieves a heading root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.48°, corresponding to a 36.0% reduction relative to the DOP-gradient-based method.

items.title: Reference-satellite dependence in wide-area PPP-RTK ionospheric modeling: a controlled comparison of undifferenced and between-satellite single-differenced STEC
items.summary: Introduction Wide-area slant total electron content (STEC) models provide regional ionospheric constraints for accelerating precise point positioning real-time kinematic (PPP-RTK). Between-satellite single differencing is widely used to eliminate receiver differential code bias (RDCB), but it also couples the quality and availability of all target-satellite constraints to a common reference satellite. Methods This study performs a controlled comparison of undifferenced STEC (UD-STEC) and between-satellite single-differenced STEC (SD-STEC) using 21 days of GPS and Galileo observations from a sparse European network. Both strategies are derived from the same PPP-AR-based ionospheric observations and evaluated with the same reference-network configuration, radial basis function interpolation, uncertainty-generation procedure, and user-side PPP-RTK processing. Consistent UD-STEC observations are recovered through GIM-assisted RDCB calibration. Results The two strategies show comparable modeling performance during quiet periods, whereas their differences become more evident as ionospheric variability increases. Over the full dataset, UD-STEC reduces the mean modeling RMS by 10.37% for GPS and 14.75% for Galileo relative to SD-STEC. During active periods, the P95 PPP-RTK convergence time decreases from 510 s with SD-STEC to 300 s with UD-STEC. items.title: APPLICATION OF POLYNOMIAL TRANSFORMATION IN GEOREFERENCE OF GRAPHIC CADASTRAL PLANS
items.summary: Polynomial transformation is a classic mathematical tool in geodesy, used to convert coordinates between different reference systems. It is mainly used in cases where the exact geometric or physical model of the relationship between the systems is unknown, as well as in the presence of significant local deformations in the source data. In practice, this method is used in: transformation between coordinate systems (including local), approximation of heights when creating geoid models, localization in GNSS measurements, as well as in specific tasks in photogrammetry and laser scanning. One of its most widespread applications remains the georeferencing of raster images. This paper investigates the specifics of applying polynomial transformation for georeferencing purposes. The main emphasis is placed on the dependence of the results on the configuration and the number of control points used. An analysis is made and recommendations are formulated for their optimal distribution on the image. The mathematical requirement for uniform grid coverage in a minimum of n+1 columns and rows (where n is the degree of the polynomial) is justified as a condition for avoiding singularity. Additionally, the negative effects of the collinearity of the control points on the computational stability are considered, as well as the approaches for identifying the Runge phenomenon (appearance of high-amplitude oscillations) in the extrapolation zones along the boundaries of the transformed range.
items.ai_summary: Discusses polynomial transformation techniques for georeferencing cadastral maps, highlighting applications in GNSS coordinate conversion and geoid modelling.

items.title: Analysis of SMAP-R Polarimetric Information for Improved Sea Surface Wind Retrieval
items.summary: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System reflectometry (GNSS-R) sea surface wind speed retrieval commonly relies on the normalized bistatic radar cross section (NBRCS), whose response depends on observation geometry, link conditions, signal quality, and sea state. Under low-wind, high-swell conditions, local wind speed alone cannot fully explain variations in reflected signals. We use SMAP-R hybrid compact polarimetric observations and ERA5 wind and wave data to assess whether polarimetric features improve sea surface wind speed retrieval. A dataset of 2,067,971 observations is divided by complete months into training, validation, calibration, and test sets. With total significant wave height included in every baseline, paired non-polarimetric and polarimetric configurations are evaluated on identical samples using a geophysical model function with minimum-variance fusion (GMF/MV), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and a fully connected network trained by back-propagation (BP-FCN). Adding the degree of polarization and normalized third Stokes component reduces the overall root mean square error (RMSE) by 7.83%, 5.49%, and 5.31%, respectively, with the polarimetric BP-FCN configuration achieving the lowest RMSE of 1.666 m s−1. Wind speed-stratified analysis shows that the relative error reduction from polarimetric information varies non-monotonically across wind speed intervals. items.title: FY-3E GNOS-II GNSS-R Level-2 (L2) Ocean Surface Wind Speed Dataset, August–October 2021
items.summary: This dataset contains organized and collocated FY-3E GNOS-II GNSS-R Level-2 (L2) ocean surface wind speed data from August to October 2021. It consists of three monthly MAT files containing GPS, BeiDou and Galileo observations, with a combined size of approximately 3.50 GB. The actual temporal coverage extends from 1 August 2021 to 31 October 2021, and the observations span approximately 63.741°S–79.240°N, with longitude expressed from 0° to 360°. The data are distributed along satellite observation tracks, with a nominal sampling frequency of 1 Hz and a nominal spatial resolution of approximately 25 km. Each file contains a double-precision N × 70 matrix named L2_process, in which each row represents one observation. The principal variables include time, location, L2 wind speed, quality flag, satellite identifiers, incidence angle, normalized bistatic radar cross section (NBRCS), signal-to-noise ratio, navigation system code, and collocated ECMWF reference wind speed. The files can be read using MATLAB or Python with h5py; chunked reading is recommended because of their large sizes.

items.title: Covariance ellipse-guided base station selection for tightly coupled PPP/INS/5G UAV positioning
items.summary: Abstract Degraded satellite geometry can lead to anisotropic position uncertainty in PPP/INS solutions. Selecting base stations solely by distance does not explicitly account for the directional characteristics of this uncertainty. To address this limitation, this study proposes a covariance ellipse–guided base station selection strategy for tightly coupled PPP/INS/5G positioning. The strategy uses the major-axis direction of the PPP/INS horizontal covariance ellipse to identify the direction of greatest position uncertainty. Four-station combinations are screened using three-dimensional geometric conditioning and predicted posterior variance constraints, and eligible combinations are ranked by giving priority to variance reduction along this direction. The method is evaluated using terrestrial UAV flight data and semi-simulated 5G ranges in a terrestrial configuration and a simulated nearshore configuration with one-sided base station geometry, each tested with and without simulated GNSS blockage. Across the four cases, the proposed solution reduces the three-dimensional root mean square (RMS) position error by 48.22%–73.94% and the 95th-percentile horizontal position error by 40.75%–74.49% relative to PPP/INS. Compared with nearest-four base station selection, the largest additional reductions are 6.31% in three-dimensional RMS error and 4.80% in the 95th-percentile horizontal error, both obtained in the terrestrial case with simulated GNSS blockage. items.title: gnss_maras: GNSS-only analysis pipeline for the 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence
items.summary: Reproducible, GNSS-only analysis of the crustal deformation produced by the 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence (Mw 7.8 Pazarcık and Mw 7.5 Elbistan–Çardak, southern Türkiye). The sequence has already been modelled with combined geodetic, seismological and remote-sensing datasets. This pipeline deliberately takes the opposite route: it asks what daily GNSS positions alone can and cannot constrain, and it calibrates every statistical test against a null model built from the same records. It estimates coseismic offsets, inverts for a depth-integrated slip distribution, measures postseismic displacement and the first-year velocity change, computes strain rates and Coulomb stress transfer, builds a moment and slip-deficit budget, and runs a search for precursory displacement whose sensitivity is established rather than assumed.

items.title: Identification of critical displacements and deformations at subsoil assets based on GNSS observation time series
items.summary: The article examines approaches to identifying critical displacements and deformations at mining assets using the GNSS observation time series. It is shown that assessing the stability of mining-engineering facilities should not be limited to analyzing absolute displacements of individual stations only, since displacements of the same magnitude may correspond to different stages of the deformation process. Existing approaches to interpretation of the displacement rates, allowable deformations, and hazard levels are reviewed based on an analysis of Russian and international publications, as well as regulatory and methodological documents. Particular attention is given to transition from assessing the kinematics of individual points to analyzing the spatial deformation field. The principal strain axes, dilatation, and maximum shear strain are proposed as informative parameters, which combined analysis makes it possible to identify zones of extension, compression, loosening, compaction, and shear strain concentration. It is shown that universal threshold criteria cannot be directly transferred to all the mining assets and should be refined with regard to the specific engineering-geological conditions, mining regime, characteristics of the monitoring network, and measurement accuracy. items.title: Comparative Analysis of BDS PPP-B2b on Shore-Based and Ship-Borne Platforms
items.summary: The integration technology of autonomous navigation and positioning provides critical technical support for high-precision positioning in the marine environment. As an indispensable core technology in modern marine navigation, satellite navigation plays a vital role in marine navigation safety and precision operations, such as marine surveying, ship navigation, and offshore engineering. The BDS PPPB2b service is commonly used in the marine high-precision application. However, compared to the landing application, the BDS PPP in the marine environment performs poorly due to the complex environmental factors on the ship-borne platform, such as hull occlusion and sea surface signal reflection. To compare and analyze the positioning performance differences of BDS PPP-B2b between shore-based and ship-borne platforms, an experiment has been conducted by using real data of the BDS receiver on both shore-based and ship-borne platforms. The results have shown that the BDS PPPB2b positioning performance on a ship-borne platform achieves poor satellite visibility and stable positioning performance. The BDS PPPB2b positioning accuracy after convergence can reach centimeter and decimeter levels on shore-based and ship-borne platforms, respectively.

It systematically reviews the development trends of the three major technical systems of satellite navigation, space-terrestrial integrated communication network, and Earth observation, pointing out that aerospace information technology is undergoing a four-dimensional observation revolution in space, time, spectrum, and elements, and shows an inevitable trend of communication-navigation-remote sensing integration. A triune empowering framework of spatiotemporal intelligence, communication intelligence, and perception intelligence is proposed, clarifying that aerospace information technology supports high-quality development through three mechanisms: factor empowerment, process intelligence, and system resilience. items.title: Effects of signal distortion biases on atmospheric delay modeling and PPP-RTK in multi-receiver-type regional networks
items.summary: Abstract Atmospheric delay modeling, comprising both ionospheric and tropospheric delays, is a crucial component for implementing PPP-RTK. Its primary task is to obtain atmospheric delays at the user end through interpolation, and then broadcast them as atmospheric augmented information to users. However, in PPP-RTK systems, multiple receiver types may be used at the server end and user end. In this case, the presence of signal distortion bias (SDB) introduces significant discrepancies between the broadcast atmospheric augmentation information and the actual atmospheric delays at the user end. This prevents users from eliminating interference caused by atmospheric delay, consequently hindering the achievement of rapid ambiguity resolution. To solve this problem, we focus on the PPP-RTK technique in multi-receiver-type regional networks, and establish a PPP-RTK system that takes into account SDB. Why it’s important: ONSMA is intended to make signals more resilient and much less subject to spoofing. It does that, but this study showed some weaknesses. Consequently, effective frequencies and ionospheric calibrations had been computed and/or stored incorrectly resulting in faulty calibrations of VLBI observations. items.title: Autonomous Navigation and Safe Landing of an Aerial Vehicle in a GPS-Denied Martian Environment
items.summary: Objectives: To develop and evaluate a real-time, low-power multi-sensor fusion framework that performs localization and safe landing-zone detection together for an aerial vehicle operating over Martian terrain, where neither GPS nor prior maps are available. Method: A stereo camera (Intel RealSense D435i), a rotating 16-beam LiDAR and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) are fused on a Raspberry Pi 5 and Pixhawk flight controller. LiDAR-assisted visual-inertial SLAM (ORB-SLAM with an Extended Kalman Filter) provides localization, while a classical computer-vision pipeline in OpenCV (CLAHE normalization, Sobel flatness analysis, mask fusion and geometric filtering) selects landing zones. The system was tested in 50 AirSim descent trials from 12 m altitude over Martian-analogue terrain with craters, rocks and dust-covered plains. Findings: Localization error remained below 4 cm, with drift under 0.6 m over 100 m; visual-inertial fusion cut drift by 45% compared with vision-only tracking. Map coverage reached 95%. The LSDS classified no-fly zones with 93% accuracy, needed 18.5 ms per frame (about 5 times faster than the CNN-based HALO approach) and guided the vehicle to within 0.3 m of the target. Landing succeeded in 98% of trials (49/50; 95% CI 89.5–99.6%) at under 10 W, against more than 20 W for GPU-based VINS-Mono at comparable accuracy. Novelty: Earlier GPS-denied SLAM and planetary landing systems address either localization or hazard assessment or depend on GPU/LiDAR-heavy

items.title: RASR: Range-Aware Scale Recovery for Metric UAV Navigation
items.summary: A central challenge in image-goal UAV navigation under Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) denial is estimating metric distance and heading between current and goal views. Dense pairwise geometry models capture relative scene structure, but without a calibrated metric scale, they cannot directly provide reliable distance estimates for navigation. Although global scale calibration corrects the dominant scale bias, the remaining errors vary systematically with distance. In this paper, Range-Aware Scale Recovery (RASR) is proposed, which complements global scale calibration with range-aware residual correction. RASR encodes pairwise geometry extracted by a frozen Matching And Stereo 3D Reconstruction (MASt3R) backbone as a compact descriptor and separates the scale-recovery core from task-specific command calibration. On the official online evaluation of the UAVs in Multimedia 2026 PairUAV challenge, our team nuaaceie achieved a total error of 0.003189 with RASR, lower than global scale calibration alone. The results demonstrate that range-aware residual correction improves metric distance estimation beyond global scale calibration. Code and materials are available at https://github.com/lht-research/rasr-pairuav.
items.ai_summary: Proposes Range-Aware Scale Recovery to improve metric UAV navigation when GNSS is denied, combining global scale calibration with range cues. Demonstrates reduced distance errors in image-goal tasks.

items.summary: Ground surface subsidence resulting from underground mining is characterized by significant spatial deformation gradients and nonlinear temporal deformation. A single monitoring technique is insufficient to simultaneously achieve extensive spatial coverage and high temporal continuity. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides high spatial resolution but is limited by sparse temporal sampling, whereas the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) offers dense temporal sampling but with restricted spatial coverage. To address these limitations, this study introduces a spatio-temporal fusion method combining InSAR and GNSS, based on baseline deformation field–residual decoupling (BR-STKF), specifically applied to the Banji Coal Mine in the Huainan Mining Area, Anhui Province. Sentinel-1 SBAS-InSAR is employed to derive Line-Of-Sight (LOS) deformation time series, while three-dimensional GNSS displacements are projected onto the LOS direction. A daily scale baseline deformation field is constructed using pixel-wise Kalman filtering and Rauch–Tung–Striebel (RTS) smoothing. Subsequently, residual signals between the InSAR/GNSS observations and the baseline field are estimated utilizing a correlation-anchored multiscale spatial basis and an information-form Kalman filter. items.title: Day-boundary discontinuity elimination method of PPP time transfer with “0 to 0” orbit and clock products
items.summary: Abstract Day-boundary discontinuities at 00:00 in daily GNSS orbit and clock products can introduce nanosecond-level jumps into precise point positioning (PPP) clock estimates and degrade the continuity of station-to-station time transfer. Leveraging recently released “0 to 0” products, this study proposes a new processing strategy that explicitly uses the precisely determined day-boundary jumps. The method first computes the satellite-wise orbit and clock discontinuities at 00:00 from two consecutive “0 to 0” files, then distributes these jumps over a short correction interval on the second day and applies a small process noise to the ionosphere-free ambiguities so that they gradually absorb the residual boundary-induced errors. The approach is implemented within a PPP time-transfer framework and evaluated using 31 days of COD final and GBM rapid products, together with GPS and Galileo observations from four IGS stations forming three time-transfer links. Conventional PPP processing produces clock jumps ranging from less than 1 ns to approximately 6 ns. For the three links, the mean absolute difference between the results at 00:00:00 and 00:00:30 decreases from 0.056-0.225 ns to 0.012-0.027 ns, corresponding to reductions of approximately 79-93%. items.title: Parallax: How a Community-Built GPS Location Changer Works — and Why It Leads
items.summary: Parallax is a tool that changes the GPS location of a phone. It runs on a computer and connects to the phone over a cable, so it does not need a jailbreak, a root, or any risky change to the phone itself. This technical overview explains what Parallax is, how a phone decides where it is, and how Parallax changes that location safely. It also covers the ideas behind the project: it is built with its community, it is priced for the people who actually use it, and its support is easy to reach, to the point that users can speak with the developer directly. Why change a phone's location Maps, games, social apps, delivery apps, and dating apps all read a phone's location and change what they show because of it. There are plenty of honest reasons to set that location on purpose. A developer may need to test how an app behaves in another country. A tester may need to check a feature that only turns on inside a certain area. A traveler may want a game or an app to keep working the way it did back home. And a privacy-minded user may simply not want every app to know exactly where they are. Parallax is a clean, deliberate way to do all of this. How a phone decides where it is A phone works out its location from a mix of signals: GPS satellites, nearby Wi-Fi networks, cell towers, and sometimes Bluetooth. In summer, the near-midnight enhancement was also present at nearly fixed locations, confirming a temporal increase, but its strength changed markedly among viewing directions and sampled regions. items.title: WayTrace: A Map-to-Language-to-Trace Hierarchy for Embodied Urban Navigation
items.summary: Web services provide walking directions for nearly every city, but following them reliably over long routes remains challenging for autonomous robots. Point-goal navigation policies rely heavily on accurate GNSS, while most vision-language navigation models struggle to execute even short instructions outdoors. We present WayTrace, a hierarchical system that connects web-map directions to robot motion through language. An off-the-shelf orchestrator vision-language model reads the turn-by-turn directions, a satellite map and recent camera images, and issues one atomic language command at a time, such as "cross the road to the left". An onboard trace predictor, trained on over one million automatically labelled samples from street-level images, draws the path for this command in the image, and a reinforcement learning policy tracks it. In long-range simulated missions, WayTrace remains robust to GNSS noise and rarely leaves crosswalks or sidewalks, while point-goal baselines degrade sharply with about ten times more violations. Deployed on a wheeled-legged robot, WayTrace completes real-world missions of up to 1.37 km at about 1.1 m/s through a busy city centre, rural trails and a university campus, handling crosswalks, staircases and construction sites. Project page: https://way-trace.github.io

items.title: The study on consistency and reliability of GNSS receiver antenna type-mean and individual phase center corrections
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   This study investigates the consistency and reliability of GNSS receiver antenna type-mean phase center corrections by analyzing both individual and type-mean Phase Center Correction (PCC) models. Using data from approximately 70 geodetic-grade antennas within the Polish ASG-EUPOS network, we quantify variations in calibration models across multiple GNSS signals. Differences between individual and type-mean calibrations are assessed in both the pattern and position domains. The analysis reveals signal-specific discrepancies, particularly for GPS L2 (G02), where deviations reach up to 5 mm in dPCC RMS and 30 mm in MAX values, impacting ionosphere-free (IF) linear-combinations. Position-domain validation via Precise Point Positioning further demonstrates vertical offsets exceeding 5 mm due to outdated or incomplete PCC models, with systematic biases arising from cross-system substitutions, e.g., GPS corrections used for GALILEO signals. The findings emphasize the need for consistent, up-to-date calibration models, and propose robust, signal-specific metrics to support the reliable use of GNSS data in regional and global reference frames.

items.title: Velocity-aided collaborative navigation for non-cooperative object localization in GNSS-denied environments
items.summary: Abstract In collaborative multi-platform observation systems, radar-based localization of non-cooperative aerial objects is often limited by obstacles, sensing-range constraints, and measurement uncertainties. Moreover, in global navigation satellite system-denied environments caused by interference, spoofing, or other disruptions, the position and velocity estimates of aircraft can be affected by significant noise. First, a velocity-aided collaborative navigation filtering algorithm using inter-node range and radial-velocity measurements is developed for multiple cooperative platforms. Subsequently, a velocity-aided localization algorithm is employed to estimate the object’s position under various measurement conditions. Finally, an interacting multiple model filtering and fusion method is utilized to fully integrate available observational information. Simulation and analysis results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the range-only baseline and several velocity-aided filtering baselines in the tested scenarios.

items.summary: Abstract Integrated navigation systems often have limited awareness of environmental changes in complex settings. When global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals are disrupted, mismatch in the measurement-noise model can substantially degrade positioning accuracy and stability. First, the IMM framework runs multiple noise models in parallel and updates their posterior probabilities using measurement innovations and prior knowledge, thereby estimating the measurement-noise covariance. The resulting estimate is then used to adaptively reconstruct the observation-information weights of the GNSS factor nodes in the factor graph. items.summary: The performance of integrated navigation using global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) and inertial navigation systems (INS) in challenging urban environments is highly dependent on the quality of GNSS observations, particularly under multipath and non-line-of-sight conditions. Conventional weighting strategies based on predefined empirical relationships with satellite elevation angle or signal quality are limited in characterizing the nonlinear and time-varying characteristics of GNSS measurement errors. To address this issue, this study proposes a deep learning-based adaptive weighting method for tightly coupled GNSS/INS integration. items.title: Trajectory Design for Timing–Range Bias Separation in GNSS-Referenced C-UAS Radar Testing
items.summary: GNSS-referenced counter-uncrewed aircraft system (C-UAS) radar evaluation depends on implementation choices and the information supplied by the test trajectory. Twenty-nine tracks from four date groups at one site were analysed, using CWA 18150 and KS W 8100 as methodological context. Detection-event and range definitions had the highest four-metric influence scores, 21.7% and 11.4%; excluding trackability reversed their order. To first order, constant radial velocity prevents separate estimation of a timing offset and a constant range bias. Offsets were estimated by fitting the time-shifted reference trajectory, because known-delay simulations showed first-order estimates biased by several seconds for 10 s offsets on curved trajectories. Offsets were identified on 19 tracks, 18 of them in a local ±5 s search, and ranged from −14.9 to +18.6 s. Adding a timing term to track-specific range biases improved the fit on every pooled date, but a single offset per date was not consistently favoured. Residuals were strongly autocorrelated, and block-bootstrap uncertainties exceeded formal standard errors by a median factor of 2.0 to 2.6, depending on block length. Radial-velocity variation, residual scale and observation count are connected to a target timing precision, and a reporting form is proposed that retains evaluation choices, corrected and uncorrected metrics, and offset uncertainty. Physical offset sources remain unresolved.

items.title: Flood extent, water level, and surface water storage retrieval using spaceborne GNSS reflectometry
items.summary:
(English) Floods are among the most frequent and destructive natural hazards worldwide. Driven by climate change and increasing human activities, the frequency and severity of flood events have increased significantly, highlighting the need for high-resolution and all-weather flood monitoring methods to improve early warning and emergency response capabilities.
Spaceborne GNSS reflectometry (GNSS-R) is an emerging microwave remote sensing technique that exploits reflected GNSS signals from the Earth’s surface to retrieve geophysical parameters at a global scale. With advantages including all-weather capability, continuous observation, and low cost, spaceborne GNSS-R shows great potential for flood monitoring. However, several challenges remain, including limited studies using multi-constellation GNSS-R observations, insufficient quantitative assessment of flood severity, and relatively coarse spatiotemporal resolution of existing flood products.
This thesis focuses on the retrieval of flood extent, water level, and surface water storage using spaceborne GNSS-R. The main contributions are summarized as follows:
(1) The sensitivity of multi-constellation GNSS-R observations to surface parameters was investigated. Results show that reflected signals from GPS, BeiDou, and Galileo exhibit comparable quality and consistent sensitivity to soil moisture, while surface reflectivity increases nonlinearly with increasing soil moisture. Period II, representing the transition from supersonic shock waves to global-scale gravity waves, exhibited a velocity of 270.6 ± 19.7 m/s. Period III, associated with atmospheric gravity waves, propagated at 253.6 ± 19.0 m/s, while period IV, linked to vertical acoustic resonance, showed a velocity of 358.2 ± 14.0 m/s. This enhancement is attributed to constructive interactions between the propagating waves and local ionospheric electrodynamics, particularly the Pre-Reversal Enhancement (PRE) phenomenon. In contrast, the near-source region is characterised by ionospheric depletion (ionospheric hole) caused by strong shock acoustic impulses. These findings highlight that the intensity of volcanic-induced ionospheric disturbances is strongly controlled by local electrodynamic conditions. items.title: Quality Assessment of Tianmu-1 GNSS Radio Occultation Refractivity over South China and Surrounding Regions During the 2024 Rainy Season
items.summary: Tianmu-1 (TM-1) provides global navigation satellite system (GNSS) radio occultation (RO) observations from four navigation systems. To support assimilation over humid South China, TM-1 refractivity was evaluated over South China and surrounding regions for April to September 2024 against ERA5, NCEP FNL, and IGRA2 radiosondes. The results show that the layer-mean differences from the analyses are within ±0.4%, statistically significant but small compared with the spread, and that the total error decreases from about 3% near the surface to 1% at 8 km and remains below 1% in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere before the spread increases again above 25 km. The data quality remains stable from month to month during the rainy season. The four constellations differ little below 20 km, but GPS and GLONASS show a 25% larger spread at 20–30 km (variance ratio 1.57, F-test p<0.001) and Galileo penetrates less deeply. Superrefractive gradients occur in about 7% of the radiosonde layers near the surface, and superrefraction-aware quality control is recommended below 8 km. These results provide a basis for specifying TM-1 observation errors in regional assimilation.

items.title: Risk-Priced Freshness Scheduling for Geohazard Early Warning over Coupled Sensor–Edge Observation Networks
items.summary: GNSS/InSAR stations, satellite fire products, UAV flood imagery and weather stations compete for the same uplink slots and edge compute. Existing Age-of-Information schedulers treat every unit of staleness as equally harmful, yet a ten-minute delay is negligible for a meteorological stream and fatal for a seismic onset. We recast freshness scheduling as risk-priced scheduling: SIV-Net predicts the geoscience value of a resource slot from link/AoI state and task descriptors, PRISM embeds freshness deadlines and a preemption penalty into a constrained MDP whose Lagrangian relaxation yields a Whittle-style index, and TANDEM couples scheduling with offload selection through a shared affinity tensor and asynchronous updates. On SMAP/MSL, Weather, EuroSAT and FloodNet, the framework reaches F1 0.9002/0.9648, MSE 0.168, accuracy 98.91% and mIoU 82.4, cutting the hazard missed-alarm rate from 2.71% to 0.96% while retaining above 89% of source-domain performance under new climate zones, sensors and seasons.

items.title: GNSS Precipitable Water Vapor Assimilation for Improving Numerical Weather Prediction of Meteorological Parameters in Small Watersheds
items.summary: Accurate short-term forecasts of meteorological parameters remain challenging in mountainous small watersheds because sparse observations and global background fields do not adequately capture rapid local water vapor variations. Previous studies indicate that assimilating GNSS-derived PWV can improve regional-scale forecasts of precipitation and near-surface meteorological variables. However, its incremental value in mountainous small watersheds remains uncertain. Complex terrain, sparse local observations, and rapid water vapor variability may limit the transferability of findings obtained over larger domains. To address this setting-specific gap, we assess the impact of GNSS-derived PWV assimilation on short-term numerical forecasts for the Shahe watershed and its surrounding area in Hanzhong, China. Using the Weather Research and Forecasting Data Assimilation (WRFDA) system, the MET experiment assimilated conventional meteorological observations from four GNSS meteorological (GNSS-Met) stations, whereas MET + PWV additionally assimilated GNSS-derived PWV from the same four stations. The 129 CMA meteorological stations were reserved exclusively for independent forecast verification. During the selected precipitation period, adding GNSS-derived PWV reduces hourly precipitation RMSE by 4.7% compared with assimilating conventional meteorological observations alone. items.title: Estimation of the NAVD88 Bias Relative to the IHRF in Mexico Using Optimized Spatial Filtering
items.summary: The estimation of the vertical datum potential in Mexico (Ŵ0NAVD88) and its geopotential bias (δŴ0) relative to the International Height Reference Frame (IHRF) is essential for integrating national vertical systems into a global reference frame. We propose a methodology based on GNSS observations, orthometric heights, and geoid undulations derived from two regional geoid models (xGGM23 and GGM25) and four high-resolution global geopotential models (WHU-CASM-UGM2025_2159, EIGEN-6C4, XGM2019e_2159, and SGG-UGM-2), combining adaptive spatial filtering with a weighting scheme that integrates spatial density and orthometric height. The results show consistent estimates of δŴ0 between −6.456 and −6.746 m2 s−2, corresponding to Ŵ0NAVD88 values between 62,636,859.856 and 62,636,860.146 m2 s−2. The formal SEM ranges from ±0.768 to ±1.060 m2 s−2 (≈8–11 cm) but quantifies formal precision only; the combined systematic error budget is ≈3.3 m2 s−2 (RSS) and exceeds the inter-model spread by an order of magnitude. Consequently, no hierarchical ranking is attributed to the six solutions. The methodology provides a reproducible framework for IHRF integration, and the reported δŴ0 values represent a national mean estimate; the spatial structure of the residuals, consistent with the documented tilt of NAVD88, will be addressed in future regional analyses.

items.title: A Tightly Coupled Magnetic-Inertial SLAM System for Field Robots
items.summary: Field robots operating in mines, tunnels, and disaster areas require reliable localization despite GNSS denial and degraded camera and LiDAR measurements caused by dust, smoke, or poor illumination. Missions involving both ground and aerial robots further motivate complementary sensing modalities that do not depend on visibility, preinstalled infrastructure, or wheel contact. This letter presents MISLAM, a tightly coupled magnetic-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping system using an IMU and a nine-magnetometer array, without relying on external odometry or platform-specific motion assumptions. The system combines the inertial navigation model with local polynomial magnetic-field models for short-term motion estimation and a global Gaussian process model for drift correction using an error-state Kalman filter. Offline evaluation on three indoor datasets collected with a handheld rig shows reductions in total endpoint closure error of 45.7% - 78.0% relative to magnetic-inertial odometry. Under poor illumination, MISLAM maintains tracking after visual-inertial odometry fails, achieving a horizontal closure error of 0.332 m, although vertical drift remains a limitation. These results support magnetic-inertial SLAM as a complementary localization modality for robotic sensor suites operating under degraded visual conditions.

items.title: The Neural Density Model: An Open 3D Thermospheric Density Reanalysis for 2003--2026 From Tracked Space Debris
items.summary: Thermospheric mass density controls satellite drag but is observed directly by few missions, and the leading operational product (HASDM) relies on non-public radar data. We present the Neural Density Model (NDM), a 3D density reanalysis for October 2003--October 2026 at 250--800~km. Previous approaches either convert the orbital decay of tracked objects into point densities or correct empirical models with a few global scale factors. NDM instead fits a spatially resolved neural correction to NRLMSISE-00 directly to the observed decay of 600--800 objects per year, through a differentiable drag operator, jointly with their ballistic coefficients, calibration spheres and accelerometer densities. On withheld satellites the median error is 0.078 (natural-log units), against 0.101 for HASDM and 0.310 for NRLMSISE-00; NDM has the smaller bias, HASDM slightly smaller scatter. On Spire GNSS orbits, never used in training, NDM and HASDM perform comparably. NDM uses only public observations.

items.title: Beyond GNSS: Leveraging LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity for Doppler Positioning
items.summary: Large constellations of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites provide ubiquitous global connectivity; yet, their rapid motion introduces significant Doppler shift effects. While challenging for communication, these effects can be leveraged for precise user terminal (UT) positioning, particularly in GNSS-denied environments where traditional satellite-based navigation struggles. Unlike GNSS, most LEO satellites lack dedicated navigation signals, motivating signals-of-opportunity (SOPs) approaches that repurpose existing LEO signals and use publicly available two-line element (TLE) files for orbital information, although ephemeris errors can limit accuracy. This article explores the fundamental principles, challenges, and enabling technologies for LEO-based Doppler shift positioning, highlighting its advantages over conventional non-Doppler methods, and discussing future research directions. Furthermore, to facilitate realistic and reproducible performance evaluation beyond stochastic modeling, we propose SionnaNTN-RT, a ray tracing framework for non-terrestrial network (NTN) built upon Sionna, enabling end-to-end simulation of Doppler-based positioning. Simulation results demonstrate that Doppler-based positioning can achieve high positioning accuracy in both urban and open-sky environments, highlighting its promise for next-generation positioning systems.

items.title: Robust 3DMA GNSS Positioning in Urban Areas Using Conservative Candidate Set Determination Based on GNSS Shadow and Reflection
items.summary: In urban environments, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning is often degraded by signal blockage and reflection caused by surrounding buildings. To address this problem, various three-dimensional mapping-aided (3DMA) GNSS techniques have been proposed. Among them, zonotope shadow and reflection matching (ZSRM) has demonstrated effective positioning performance by determining the candidate receiver position set using predicted GNSS shadow and reflection regions. However, ZSRM remains vulnerable to satellite signal misclassification, which may lead to positioning failure. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a conservative candidate set determination strategy for robust ZSRM positioning. items.title: A shipborne GNSS spoofing detection algorithm based on temporally constrained prior-association
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Ship navigation relies on the global navigation satellite system (GNSS), but civil GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing attacks that can induce erroneous positioning results. Existing inertial- and sensor-based methods usually describe the consistency between GNSS information and measurements from non-GNSS sensors through direct motion comparison, filter innovations, or test statistics derived from acceleration constraints, but they do not fully characterize the temporal association changes in the motion inconsistency caused by spoofing attacks in maritime scenarios. We propose a shipborne GNSS spoofing detection algorithm based on temporally constrained prior-association. Orientation is estimated by fusing an inertial measurement unit (IMU) and a gyrocompass, with the observation noise covariance of the normalized gravity vector adaptively adjusted according to the gravity magnitude deviation. The IMU acceleration is transformed into the navigation frame, and the residual between the second-order-differenced GNSS acceleration and the IMU acceleration is used as the input sequence. A transformer detection framework is then constructed by introducing a prior-association weight matrix jointly constrained by temporal distance and temporal position into multi-head attention. The symmetrized Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the series-association and prior-association matrices is combined with reconstruction error to form the anomaly score.

items.title: South of the 2016 rupture termination: Geodetic constraints on coseismic slip of the 2026 M7.1 Kumamoto Earthquake

Slip decreases toward the southwest, where weak slip remains at shallow depth on the southwestern segment; cross-validation tests and a strong-motion waveform inversion supported its robustness. items.title: The 2025 Mw 7.7 Myanmar Earthquake: Finite Fault Versus Point Source in Modeling Coseismic Ionospheric Disturbances

The source is a moment-weighted distribution of sub-sources along the fault, each radiating at its own rupture time. items.title: Reevaluating Large‐Scale Deformation Precursors of Great Subduction Earthquakes: Insights From Satellite Gravity and GNSS Data
items.summary: Abstract Validating the controversial hypothesis that precursory gravity changes arise from sudden acceleration of subducting plates potentially triggering great earthquakes is of paramount importance. To rigorously evaluate proposed precursors for the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku and 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule earthquakes, we develop a statistical framework that enables (a) robust assessment of their statistical significance, (b) characterization of temporal evolution, and (c) integrative analysis across multiple GRACE gravity solutions with differing error characteristics. Additionally, we test the precursor hypothesis using independent GNSS‐measured surface displacements within a physically consistent framework. Our results show no evidence supporting the proposed precursor in either alternative GRACE solutions or high‐precision GNSS observations. The anomalous gravity changes previously interpreted as earthquake precursors are indistinguishable from solution‐specific data errors or other non‐tectonic signals, lacking evidence for tectonic origin.

items.title: GNSS Receiver Operating Point Comparison Between Vector and Scalar Tracking Under High-Dynamics
items.summary: This paper presents a measurement noise adaptation mechanism for Kalman filter-based carrier tracking in a navigation-aided GNSS receiver designed for launch-vehicle applications. The tracking loop is tuned for 20\,g acceleration steps, which requires a wide bandwidth that makes the loop vulnerable to noise-driven pull-out at low carrier-to-noise density ratios. To resolve this tradeoff, the measurement noise covariance, $R$, is inflated via a two-layer gate: a sigmoid envelope keyed to the signal $C/N_0$, modulated by a dynamics indicator derived from the discriminator output statistics of the Loop Bandwidth Control Algorithm. During noise-dominated periods the gate inflates~$R$, reducing the Kalman gain so the filter coasts on the navigation-aided prediction; when dynamics are detected the gate opens within one epoch, restoring the high-bandwidth tuning. The navigation aiding is formulated as a stochastic control input whose uncertainty is propagated from the navigation EKF covariance. Simulation results on a 20\,g acceleration step scenario show that the adapted vector architecture doubles the lock-retention rate relative to the standalone scalar filter at $C/N_0 = 31$\,dB-Hz. The receiver is implemented in MSGR, an open-source MATLAB GNSS software-defined receiver.

Abstract

In unstructured natural environments, such as rivers, this is challenging as vegetated riverbanks and tree-canopy occlusion can degrade Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) reception, which in turn degrades the vehicle's Inertial Navigation System (INS)/GNSS navigation solution, worsening its position, velocity, and attitude estimates. This paper proposes an INS/GNSS/Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) architecture based on an error state Kalman filter, in which double-differenced GNSS measurements are tightly coupled, while velocity and attitude from a lightweight, scan-matching-based Iterative Closest Point (ICP) LiDAR odometry are loosely coupled. This odometry avoids reliance on both large local maps, and discernible geometric features, since water absorption and foliage scattering produce sparse, feature-poor point clouds. The proposed method is evaluated on two real-world airborne datasets from natural environments and compared against standalone Post-Processed Kinematic positioning, a state-of-the-art factor-graph approach, and a filter-based feature-dependent method. items.title: Source Mechanism of the Mw 6.4 Nicobar earthquake of July 28, 2025: constraints from GNSS and strong motion accelerograph observations
items.summary:
Abstract 
                 On 28th July 2025, a strong (Mw 6.4) earthquake occurred west of Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman Sumatra subduction zone, which is experiencing high seismicity and large postseismic deformation following the 2004 Sumatra Andaman earthquake (Mw 9.2). The earthquake probably did not cause a tsunami or any damage to the nearest town, Campbell Bay, located ~ 100 km from the epicentre. In the absence of local broadband seismic data, we estimate the source mechanism of this earthquake using high-frequency GNSS and strong-motion accelerograph (SMA) data from sites within 500 km of the earthquake in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Despite a large azimuthal gap in the observation sites, the estimated focal mechanism is consistent with that reported in global catalogues. It implies that sparsely distributed local GNSS sites, even with large azimuthal gaps, can reliably estimate earthquake source mechanisms. Thus, including these data may help rapidly assess tsunami hazard from future such earthquakes in the Andaman-Nicobar region.

items.title: A robust visual localization framework for UAVs using a zero-shot aerial-satellite image matcher and a particle filter
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Positioning of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) normally relies on the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). However, GNSS signals are prone to blockage, interference, and spoofing, which can cause positioning failures and severely degrade mission performance. Aerial-satellite image matching using intelligent methods (e.g., deep neural networks) has emerged as a promising approach for achieving meter-level absolute positioning accuracy in GNSS-denied environments. To advance localization based on aerial-satellite image matching, we propose a robust localization framework that integrates a zero-shot aerial-satellite image matcher, termed the Generalizable Image Matcher (GIM), with a particle filter. First, the front-end visual odometry estimates the UAV trajectory from consecutive onboard images to produce an initial pose. Next, guided by the front-end estimate, candidate locations are sampled to crop the corresponding satellite sub-images. GIM is then used to match aerial and satellite images and infer absolute location cues. Finally, an adaptive weighting function is designed to fuse the front-end and back-end localization information, thereby yielding the final positioning result. Experiments were conducted using data collected along 12 flight trajectories spanning rural, urban, and farmland scenarios. Assuming that the initial position of each trajectory is known, the proposed method achieved an overall average positioning error of 5.02 m a

items.title: A Hybrid Positioning Solution for Machine Control in GPS-Denied Environments: Combining Robotic Total Stations and Gyro Compasses
items.summary:
Abstract 
                   Modern machine control systems rely on GNSS-based positioning integrated with onboard tilt and inertial sensors to enable high-precision excavation, grading, dredging, and earthmoving operations. However, dependence on satellite-derived position and heading limits operational continuity in environments where GNSS signals are degraded or unavailable. The objective of this work is to develop a GNSS- independent machine control architecture capable of maintaining real-time guidance using existing survey and machine control infrastructure without modification of core machine systems. 
                   A hybrid positioning framework was developed by integrating a Robotic Total Station (RTS), a Survey- Grade Gyro Compass, and an existing machine control platform. The RTS is established on a surveyed control network and continuously tracks a 360-degree prism mounted on the excavator, generating realtime three-dimensional coordinates. The Gyro Compass provides continuous true-north-referenced heading independent of GNSS and magnetic interference. A dedicated integration layer performs realtime synchronization, coordinate transformation, and formatting of RTS-derived position and gyro- derived heading into a machine-control-compatible data stream. The fused outputs are combined with onboard kinematic sensors to compute machine geometry, including boom, stick, and bucket tip positions, enabling a deterministic positioning loop within the existing control

items.title: Integrated Monitoring of Sea State: Data analysis and System Measurements
items.summary: Knowledge of the sea state is essential for safe navigation, marine operations, and offshore and coastal engineering, yet conventional measurement relies on fixed wave buoys, which are costly to deploy and provide information only at a single location. This thesis investigates the use of a ship in navigation as a sea-state sensor, estimating wave characteristics from the vessel's measured motion response through an onboard inertial navigation system (INS) integrated with GNSS antennas. The work first establishes the theoretical background on sea waves and sea-state description, including linear wave theory, wave spectra, and standard sea-state parameters, followed by the theory of ship motion in waves, covering six-degree-of-freedom dynamics, linear seakeeping, response amplitude operators (RAOs), and the effect of encounter frequency. These foundations frame the central difficulty of the problem: unlike a buoy, which is designed to follow the sea surface, a ship filters and modifies the wave excitation through its geometry, mass distribution, and forward speed, so its vertical motion cannot be taken directly as a measure of wave height. The measurement system is then validated and calibrated under controlled dry conditions, using a pendulum to reproduce buoy-like oscillations and assess the accuracy of the inertial and GNSS sensors and of the spectral processing chain developed for this work. items.title: Dem-assisted visual geolocation integrating ephemeris-based orientation correction with Multi-Scale skyline features
items.summary: Accurate geolocation in GNSS-denied mountainous environments remains a significant challenge for navigation and field operations. While vision-based methods using terrain features like skylines offer a promising passive solution, their performance is often hindered by unknown camera orientation, low feature discriminability across vast areas, and severe degradation under nighttime conditions. To address these limitations, this paper presents a novel visual geolocation framework that synergistically couples ephemeris-based orientation correction with multi-scale skyline feature matching. First, an Edge-Enhanced SegFormer-B3 (EESFormer-B3) network is developed for robust skyline extraction from query images, where a lightweight Edge Gate mechanism is integrated to refine boundary precision, particularly under low-light scenarios. Second, we propose a camera heading estimation method utilizing solar and lunar ephemeris, eliminating reliance on external heading sensors and drastically reducing the matching search space. Third, for matching, a hierarchical composite feature is designed, encoding the skyline’s global shape trends, local directional variations, and dominant structural distributions to ensure robustness against repetitive terrain patterns. Extensive experiments were conducted in a complex 700 km 2 mountainous region. The results demonstrate that our method achieves a localization success rate of 82 % (daytime) and 76 % (nighttime) within a 250-meter error threshold.

It contains the main session, CB-11 (22 minutes, the whole of the Campinas B orchard), the calibration of the platform, a tape survey of 106 trunks that serves as a GNSS-independent reference for evaluating localization and maps, together with the LiDAR map in whose frame the trunk centres are given, and 210 images with labelled weeds and trunks (180 for training and validation and a 30-frame test set). To protect the location of the private orchards, the GNSS fixes in the recordings were moved to a synthetic origin at latitude 0, longitude 0: their timing and relative geometry are preserved, but not the absolute position. Each session also includes the track in local East–North–Up coordinates. items.title: Reply on RC3
items.summary: Abstract. Tropical cyclone (TC) inner-core vector wind fields are essential for intensity forecasting, storm surge prediction, and structural climatology. The Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) constellation provides dense temporal sampling and L-band precipitation-penetrating capability over the tropical belt, but its sparse, scalar wind speed retrievals have not been fully assimilated to produce kilometre-scale TC inner-core vector wind fields with global multi-basin coverage. This paper presents the QiFeng-CYGNSS dataset, which combines CYGNSS observations with a physics-guided score-based diffusion assimilation framework to reconstruct spatially complete 10 m vector wind fields from sparse scalar wind speed observations. The dataset covers 249 TCs across six active global basins during January 2020–September 2022, providing 1.5 km resolution vector wind fields at every IBTrACS reporting time with available CYGNSS coverage (4955 snapshots in total), accompanied by observation metadata and pixel-level ensemble uncertainty estimates for 138 major-hurricane snapshots. Independent validation against spaceborne C-band synthetic aperture radar, airborne Tail Doppler Radar, and GPS dropsondes indicates that the reconstructions represent TC inner-core structures at kilometre scales, reducing the absolute Vmax bias relative to ERA5 and CCMP by ~79% and ~75%, respectively, on the full sample. The dataset is freely available from Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zen

items.summary: ABSTRACT Most GPS interferometric reflectometry (GPS‐IR) studies use geodetic RHCP antennas with near‐hemispherical coverage and select the reflection zone through elevation and azimuth masks during processing. This study investigates directional GPS‐IR observations using a linearly polarized double‐ridged horn antenna (DRHA), which constrains the observation geometry at the acquisition stage. items.title: Global Ionospheric Responses to Four X‐Class Solar Flares in November 2025
items.summary: Abstract We investigate global ionospheric responses to four X‐class solar‐disk flares that occurred in November 2025 from the same solar active region, using multi‐instrument observations including GNSS, ionosonde, geomagnetic and GOES solar irradiance data. A consistent time delay of 30–60 s is identified between peaks in EUV irradiance rate and rate of TEC (ROT), supporting the primary role of EUV radiation in the E/F‐region TEC enhancements. In contrast, no detectable TEC response was observed for flare #1 (X1.7), despite its higher GOES X‐ray class, common active‐region origin, and similar disk location to flare #2. items.title: A Hybrid Neural-Assisted Unscented Kalman Filter for Unmanned Ground Vehicle Navigation
items.summary: Modern autonomous navigation for unmanned ground vehicles relies on different estimators to fuse inertial sensors and GNSS measurements. However, the constant noise covariance matrices often struggle to account for dynamic real-world conditions.In this work we propose a hybrid estimation framework that bridges classical state estimation foundations with modern deep learning approaches. Instead of altering the fundamental unscented Kalman filter equations, a dedicated deep neural network is developed to predict the process and measurement noise uncertainty directly from raw inertial and GNSS measurements. We present a sim2real approach, with training performed only on simulative data. In this manner, we offer perfect ground truth data and relieves the burden of extensive data recordings. To evaluate our proposed approach and examine its generalization capabilities, we employed a 160-minutes test set from three datasets each with different types of vehicles (off-road vehicle, passenger car, and mobile robot), inertial sensors, road surface, and environmental conditions. We demonstrate across the three datasets a position improvement of $12.7\%$ compared to the adaptive model-based approach. Thus, offering a scalable and a more robust solution for unmanned ground vehicles navigation tasks.

items.title: A Decoupled Variational Bayesian Adaptive Kalman Filter for MEMS INS/GNSS Integrated Navigation under Time-Varying Noise Covariances
items.summary: We evaluate a decoupled variational Bayesian adaptive Kalman filter (D-VBAKF) for MEMS INS/GNSS navigation, combining bounded fading-memory covariance matching for R with motion-regularized Bayesian model averaging over scaled Q candidates. In 50 paired trials of a 15-state, 120 s prescribed-noise simulation, 3D position RMSE reductions versus EKF-Fixed were 2.94 m (nominal paired 95% interval [1.59, 4.29] m) for 10 s outages and 7.76 m ([1.51, 14.02] m) for 30 s outages. At 60 s, intervals versus EKF-Fixed and joint-VB VBAKF included zero; all 90 s intervals included zero. In the separate no-outage simulation, Q-KL was 0.011, and the R relative error was 0.173. On one 1617 s ICM20602 drive with deterministic GNSS perturbations, full-route 3D RMSE was 27.19 m versus 30.77 m for EKF-Fixed. Across twelve repeated outage windows on that drive, the R-only variant yielded 28.19 m versus 28.86 m for the full method; BMA-Q only yielded 33.98 m versus 33.23 m for EKF-Fixed. Thus, the real-data experiment did not demonstrate an incremental accuracy benefit from adding BMA-Q to R-only adaptation, and validation on a single drive limits the generalizability of the findings. NIS coverage was 0.636 for D-VBAKF and 0.626 for EKF-Fixed, both below the nominal 0.95.

items.title: Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Computational Geodetic Inversion: A Review and Framework for Multi-Source Earth Observation
items.summary: Geodetic inversion converts surface and remote sensing data into estimates of concealed Earth system parameters, including fault slip, magma-source geometry, subsurface mass changes, crustal strain, and time-dependent geohazard activities. This review explores geodetic inversion as a computational challenge that involves combining diverse data, optimizing and quantifying uncertainty, and providing explainable decision support. A narrative technical review was compiled using literature records from Scopus and Dimensions on topics such as geodetic inversion, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), gravity and seismic source modeling, Bayesian inversion, sparse regularization, and physics-informed learning. The literature was sorted based on the data types, inverse-problem structures, algorithmic groups, uncertainty management, and reporting standards. This review highlights five common computational layers in contemporary geodetic inversion: data harmonization, forward-model encoding, inversion and optimization, uncertainty propagation, and explainable decision support. These layers are synthesized into an explainable artificial intelligence-uncertainty quantification-computational geodetic inversion (XAI-UQ-CGI) framework for multi-source Earth observation. items.title: InSAR constraints on spatiotemporal changes in plate coupling beneath Shikoku along the Nankai subduction zone
items.summary: Abstract Estimating spatiotemporal changes in plate coupling is important for understanding the nucleation processes of megathrust earthquakes. Using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) observations, we obtained crustal deformation around Shikoku, southwest Japan, from 2014 to 2025. We estimated slip deficit distributions along the Nankai subduction zone using kinematic fault slip inversions based on GNSS, InSAR, and GNSS-InSAR joint observations. Both the GNSS- and InSAR-based slip deficit models showed that slip deficit rates beneath central Shikoku decreased by up to 41 mm/year after 2019 relative to 2014–2018. We interpret this as a weakening of plate coupling rather than a long-term slow slip event, because the estimated slip deficit rates were not significantly negative even after 2019. Our results demonstrate that InSAR-derived velocities, which are sensitive to vertical displacements, can independently constrain broad-scale changes in plate coupling beneath inland regions, although they do not drastically improve the spatial resolution of plate coupling estimates. These findings suggest that InSAR observations provide valuable information on plate coupling changes, particularly in subduction zones where dense GNSS observations are unavailable.

items.title: Investigating the interseismic coupling degree and the seismic moment accumulation rate of the Northern Apennines arc buried beneath the Po Plain in Emilia-Romagna region, (Italy)
items.summary: Summary The Emilia-Romagna portion of the Po Plain (Italy) hosts part of the outermost sector of the Northern Apennines orogenic front. The low strain-rate and the shortening gradient acting in these areas are well documented by means of recent studies, although it is still unclear which fault segment plays the dominant role in accommodating the deformation during the interseismic period. A fraction of this strain was released during the seismic sequence in Emilia-Romagna with mainshocks the May 20 and 29, 2012 (Mw 6.0 and ∼5.8, respectively), which several authors primarily attributed to two major segments of the Ferrara Arc fault system. In this work, we propose a comprehensive kinematic block modeling approach that integrates available information on fault geometry and GNSS data to identify the fault segments that most effectively accommodate the ongoing contractional geodetic velocity gradient through long-term uniform slip-rates. We therefore discretize the proposed fault model using a 3D triangular dislocation element (TDE) mesh to estimate the spatial distribution of slip-deficit rate. items.title: Smart Farm Fence Monitoring and Intrusion Detection System with AI-Based Location Track-ing: A Review and Conceptual Architecture
items.summary: Crop damage and theft caused by wild animals, stray animals and human intruders remain a persistent problem for farmers, and a passive fence neither detects nor reports a breach. This paper presents a focused narrative review of verified studies on intrusion detection, edge artificial intelligence (AI) and location tracking for farm protection, giving priority to IEEE journal publications and supplementing them with IEEE conference and open-access sources. Four themes are examined: camera-based AI detection and deterrence; low-cost sensor-triggered and LoRa-based fog or edge systems; GNSS and LoRa-based position tracking of animals; and validation practice. The reviewed work shows that lightweight deep-learning detectors can run on low-power edge devices, that a PIR-and-camera strategy has been reported to save energy, and that signal-strength information can reduce the energy spent on continuous GPS. However, the accessible evidence is dominated by prototype-scale studies, location tracking is rarely integrated with intrusion detection, and false-alarm rate, detection latency and independent validation are seldom reported. The paper contributes a comparative table of representative studies, a proposed seven-layer conceptual architecture for a smart farm fence that combines IR/PIR sensing, camera-based AI, GPS-collar tracking and geofencing, a leakage-resistant evaluation protocol, and a prioritised list of research gaps. items.title: Geocenter sensitivity from satellite tracking
items.summary: Abstract. In this study, we revisit Kaula’s orbit perturbation theory to establish how satellite orbital geometry controls the sensitivity to degree-1 gravitational signals associated with geocenter motion along the z-axis and the (x, y )-plane, respectively. We explicitly derive the Kaula-based expressions for the degree-1 potential terms and provide complete tables of the corresponding inclination and eccentricity functions for all relevant degree-1 terms. As a case study, we apply this framework to the upcoming ESA Genesis mission, which will be the first in-orbit geodetic observatory carrying all four geodetic techniques (GNSS, SLR, DORIS and VLBI) onboard. We examine the dependence of the spacecraft orbital parameters through contributions at the spacecraft location of the degree-1 gravitational potential (V10 and V11). Our analysis shows that the V10 term associated with the geocenter’s z-component scales with sin i, implying that polar orbits maximize sensitivity to vertical geocenter variations, whereas equatorial orbits remain largely insensitive to them. items.title: Evolution of Summit Magma Pressure During the 2018 Caldera Collapse at Kīlauea Volcano
items.summary: Abstract We utilized geodetic data from the 16 May to 4 August 2018 caldera collapse sequence to refine the geometries and pressure evolution of two summit reservoirs at Kīlauea volcano: the shallower Halema‘uma‘u (HMM) and deeper South Caldera (SC) reservoirs. We modeled magma reservoirs as pressurized spheroidal cavities and constrained reservoir geometries with Global Positioning System (GPS) and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar displacements. Inverting high‐rate GPS and borehole tilt time series recovered time‐dependent reservoir pressure changes and caldera ring fault shear stress. During the collapse sequence, the HMM reservoir accommodated episodic, co‐collapse pressure increases of 1.9 MPa (median) and a net 5.8 MPa (median) decrease. Simultaneously, the SC reservoir underwent monotonic depressurization of 6.7 MPa (median). Negligible co‐collapse pressure changes in the SC reservoir imply it was not exclusively supplying magma to the eruption vent. These results provide a coherent view of magma reservoir pressure evolution during the 2018 eruption.

items.title: Improving Smartphone Pedestrian Positioning in Urban Canyons Through PDR-Constrained GNSS Shadow Matching
items.summary: Smartphone global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning in building-obstructed environments is degraded by non-line-of-sight reception and multipath. Visibility-based shadow matching (SM) exploits three-dimensional building models to constrain cross-street position but has limited along-street observability. This study proposes a pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR)-constrained SM framework with two implementations: extended Kalman filter fusion (EKF-PDR/SM) using heading-orthogonal candidate search and anisotropic SM measurement uncertainty, and PDR-driven SM using candidate propagation, visibility scoring, and GNSS-proximity weighting. Evaluation used one smartphone and one pedestrian completing one traversal of each of two campus routes with different satellite-visibility conditions. Under common PDR prediction and process-noise settings, EKF-PDR/SM achieved cross-street/along-street root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 3.57/8.28 m on Route 1 and 2.46/7.83 m on Route 2, compared with 5.23/8.98 m and 4.29/12.38 m for EKF-PDR/GNSS, respectively. PDR-driven SM achieved the lowest directional RMSEs among the six compared methods: 2.92/7.47 m on Route 1 and 1.54/5.89 m on Route 2. All errors were evaluated relative to common model-derived reference trajectories. These controlled results support the use of PDR constraints to improve visibility-based SM under the tested conditions.

items.summary: Errors in GPS receivers arise from multiple sources, including thermal noise, antenna phase center variations, inter-channel and inter-frequency biases, and receiver clock offsets relative to GPS time. A major challenge is estimating inter-frequency biases (IFBs) for stations outside the International GNSS Service (IGS) network, where predefined IFB products are unavailable. This limitation introduces significant uncertainty in bias correction and degrades the accuracy of derived positioning solutions. Reliable estimation of receiver IFBs for non-IGS stations is therefore essential to maintain precise positioning performance. In this work, we introduce the IFB Estimation Using Regional Modeling (IFBERM) framework, which enables single-station estimation and comparative Analysis of satellite and receiver IFBs across various GNSS receiver architectures over Egypt by combining three regional ionospheric models (GTSM, SCHM, and polynomial). The proposed method estimates satellite and receiver Instrumental Frequency Biases (IFBs) using the Generalized Trigonometric Series Model (GTSM) and a polynomial model applied to standalone dual-frequency carrier-smoothed GPS Pseudorange measurements via elevation-weighted least squares. items.title: Search and Rescue in Tunnels, an Integrated Approach Using Robotic Platforms
items.summary: Abstract Underground infrastructure such as road and railway tunnels requires reliable communication, localisation, and situational awareness, particularly during search and rescue operations. This article summarises developments carried out within the A‑IQ Ready project in three closely related areas: underground wireless communication modeling, survivor detection, and robotic localisation. A tunnel-specific wireless simulation platform was developed and validated against measurements acquired at the underground facility Zentrum am Berg, enabling realistic prediction of quality-of-service metrics and supporting AI-based communication assessment. Measurement campaigns with a robotic platform were used to generate datasets and calibrate simulation models. For the detection of tunnel users or survivors, a multimodal thermal-LiDAR perception pipeline was implemented on the SPIDER unmanned ground vehicle (UGV). In parallel, LiDAR-based SLAM approaches were investigated for GNSS-denied tunnel environments, resulting in a centralised multi-robot mapping architecture based on LIO-SAM and map-merging concepts. Demonstrations at Zentrum am Berg confirmed the suitability of the developed technologies for search and rescue applications in complex underground infrastructure. They constitute key constituents of enhanced robotic assistance in underground emergency cases.
items.ai_summary: Explores robotic search and rescue in tunnels, focusing on underground wireless communications, survivor detection, and GNSS-denied robotic localization.

items.title: Experimental Study of the Positioning Accuracy of GNSS RTK Systems
items.summary: Despite significant advances in terrestrial cellular network (4G LTE, 5G NR), and WiFi wireless local area network (WLAN) location services in recent years, centimeter-accurate real-time positioning services across federal geographic areas are currently available exclusively through global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) with differential correction systems (DCS). The most widely used GNSS systems are those with Real Time Kinematic (RTK) DCS. Geodetic-grade GNSS RTK hardware and software systems (HSS) with subscriptions to reference base station network services, in addition to high-quality hardware for receiving primary measurements, operate using proprietary software implementing highly efficient secondary post-processing algorithms, enabling millimeter-accurate coordinate estimates (CAE) in real time. In addition to high line-of-sight (LOS) accuracy, survey-grade GNSS RTK systems effectively compensate for multipath effects in full NLOS (Non-LOS) or partial Obstructed-LOS (OLOS) scenarios, where there is no direct line of sight between the rover antenna and GNSS satellites. More affordable and mass-produced consumer GNSS RTK devices cannot achieve comparable accuracy in either LOS or NLOS scenarios. Improving the positioning accuracy of consumer GNSS RTK systems by postprocessing primary GNSS measurements in the RTKLIB open-source library is a pressing and sought-after task.
